**USCGC _Dione_ (WPC-107)** was a [_Thetis_-class patrol boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thetis-class_patrol_boat "Thetis-class patrol boat") operated by the [United States Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard "United States Coast Guard") from 1934 to 1963; she was designated a [cutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard_Cutter "United States Coast Guard Cutter"). Her and the other members of the _Thetis_ class were designed to enforce [Prohibition in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States") by stopping [rum-runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rum-running "Rum-running"); her class had been designed to improve on the experiences of previous cutters. Built by the [Manitowoc Shipbuilding Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitowoc_Shipbuilding_Company "Manitowoc Shipbuilding Company") in [Manitowoc, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitowoc,_Wisconsin "Manitowoc, Wisconsin"), _Dione_ was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") in November 1933, [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") in June 1934, and [commissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning#Commissioning "Ship commissioning") in October. Prohibition had been repealed in December 1933, so the cutter instead conducted [search and rescue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_and_rescue "Search and rescue") operations out of her station in [Norfolk, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk,_Virginia "Norfolk, Virginia").

At the outbreak of the [Second Happy Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Happy_Time "Second Happy Time") in January 1942, _Dione_ became the only large ship in the [Fifth Naval District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_naval_district#Fifth_Naval_District "United States naval district") capable of opposing German [U-boats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U-boat "U-boat"). The cutter patrolled the waters off [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina"), which were nicknamed "[Torpedo Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_Alley "Torpedo Alley")" due to the high capacity of U-boats operating there. From January to June 1942, she rescued the survivors of torpedoed ships, escorted [Allied convoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Allied_convoys_during_World_War_II_by_region#North_American_coastal_and_Caribbean_convoys "List of Allied convoys during World War II by region") passing through Torpedo Alley, and hunted sonar pings suspected to have come from U-boats with the goal of sinking one—though the cutter never sank one. In 1945, she was transferred to [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England") with two of her sister ships to help escort surrendered U-boats to American ports, which she did in May when she escorted [_U-1228_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-1228 "German submarine U-1228") to [Portsmouth, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth,_New_Hampshire "Portsmouth, New Hampshire").

_Dione_ served out of Norfolk until she was [decommissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning#Decommissioning "Ship commissioning") in July 1947 due to a lack of personnel. She was recommissioned in February 1951 and became the first Coast Guard Cutter to be stationed in [Freeport, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeport,_Texas "Freeport, Texas"). She operated in the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"), serving in a search and rescue capacity until she was once more decommissioned in February 1963. The cutter was [placed in reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_fleet "Reserve fleet") for about a year before being sold as a supply ship in March 1964.

She was operated as [a merchant ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#Commercial_service) in the [Gulf Coast region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_of_the_United_States "Gulf Coast of the United States") by three companies and under four different names. She was first known as _**Dione**_ and was operated by the Palmer Decker Boat Company until it was dissolved in September 1967; _Dione_ was seized by a [US Marshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marshals_Service "United States Marshals Service") and auctioned off in December. She was known as _**Big Trouble**_ and owned by Big Trouble Inc. until the company changed its name to Delta Boats Inc. in February 1968, and the ship's name was changed to _**Delta I**._ She was sold to Sabik Inc. in March. _Delta I_ caught fire the next month while underway in the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea"), and only her [hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_(watercraft) "Hull (watercraft)") was salvageable from the fire. The ship was rebuilt, temporarily seized by a US Marshal, and was underway again by March 1970; her name had been changed to _**Al Rashid**_ by that time. She operated under Sabik until 1992, when the former _Dione_ was last seen in service as _Al Rashid_.

[![Image 7: USS Brant (AMc-63), a motor minesweeper, anchored, sailing in the sea](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/USCGC_Jackson_%28WPC-142%29.jpg/250px-USCGC_Jackson_%28WPC-142%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USCGC_Jackson_(WPC-142).jpg)

[USCGC _Jackson_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Jackson "USCGC Jackson") in 1927. She was a member of the 125-foot (38 m) _Active_-class patrol boats that preceded the _Thetis_ class.

On 17 January 1920, the [Volstead Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volstead_Act "Volstead Act") went into force in the United States. The law executed the [Eighteenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Eighteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), which had been ratified on 16 January 1919. The amendment banned the "manufacture, sale, or transportation" of most alcohol and began the period of [Prohibition in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5): 11  The Volstead Act was enforced by local [police departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police "Police"), the [Bureau of Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Prohibition "Bureau of Prohibition"), the [US Customs Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Customs_Service "United States Customs Service"), the [Department of the Treasury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury "United States Department of the Treasury"), and the Coast Guard.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5): 11  The Coast Guard's role was to prevent [seaborne alcohol smuggling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rum-running#The_ships "Rum-running"), a job that was initially deemed small and manageable. However, by 1924, the Coast Guard was overwhelmed by the volume of smugglers and struggled to intercept more than five percent of the flow of alcohol.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5): 161-164

Alongside its normal duties, the Coast Guard shifted to impose a [blockade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockade "Blockade") along 5,000 miles (8,000 km) of American coastline. For the role, new patrol boats and [destroyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer")—which had formerly been operated by the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy")—joined the fleet to patrol at sea; Prohibition enforcement had become the first priority for the Coast Guard.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5): 161-164  While the vessels helped fill gaps off the coast, they were expensive to operate and performed poorly. In the 1920s, the Coast Guard began to build purpose-built patrol boats to take over the role of Prohibition enforcement.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383  These new cutters varied in size and capability but were used to create a continuous buffer of Prohibition enforcement that stretched from the open ocean to inner harbors.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:4-7): 89, 95, 99, 105

A common tactic by smugglers was to use large, seagoing, [mother ships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother_ship "Mother ship") that loitered off the coast and supplied alcohol to smaller boats; the smaller boats then brought the drinks ashore.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:4-7): 108  The Coast Guard ordered the construction of the 125 ft (38 m)-long [_Active_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active-class_patrol_boat "Active-class patrol boat") cutters in the 1920s to trail and intercept mother ships, and the experience was used to develop the next class of sea-going cutters.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8): 166  The 165-foot (50 m) "B"-class,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8): 166 [[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-blcassref-9) named for the cutters' [overall length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overall_length "Overall length")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) and primarily known as the [_Thetis_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thetis-class_patrol_boat "Thetis-class patrol boat"), was ordered in the 1930s and designed based on results of the _Active_ class' experiences.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8): 166  The design was intended to balance speed, [seaworthiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seakeeping "Seakeeping"), range, radio equipment, and armament.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-10): 100  Eighteen _Thetis_-class cutters were built, and they were large and fast enough to intercept the mother ships.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:4-7): 108  A newspaper article in the _[Oshkosh Northwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oshkosh\_Northwestern "Oshkosh Northwestern")_ praised the class the day before the launching of _Dione_ and two of her sisters, describing the cutters as having "the latest developments in [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_engineering "Marine engineering") and [electrical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering") together with a large cruising radius and extreme [seaworthiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seakeeping "Seakeeping")."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:37-11): 4

The Eighteenth Amendment was [repealed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repeal_of_Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Repeal of Prohibition in the United States") on 5 December 1933 with the [Twenty-first Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-first_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-first Amendment to the United States Constitution")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:3-12)—a little under a year before _Dione_ was commissioned.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) The cutter never operated in the capacity that she and her sister ships were constructed for: enforcing Prohibition in the United States.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8): 166

[![Image 8: The hulks of three ships sit on land next to the water, waiting to be launched](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/USCGCs_Dione%2C_Electra%2C_and_Pandora.png/250px-USCGCs_Dione%2C_Electra%2C_and_Pandora.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USCGCs_Dione,_Electra,_and_Pandora.png)

_Dione_ (left) on the [ways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slipway#Slipways_in_ship_construction "Slipway"), alongside her sister ships _Electra_ and _Pandora_

[![Image 9: A close-up photo of the hulk of an individual ship](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/46/Dione_on_the_ways.png/250px-Dione_on_the_ways.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dione_on_the_ways.png)

A close-up of _Dione_

[Hull number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_number "Hull number") 277,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-13): 30  listed as patrol boat 13,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:26-14): 318  was built by the [Manitowoc Shipbuilding Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitowoc_Shipbuilding_Company "Manitowoc Shipbuilding Company") in [Manitowoc, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitowoc,_Wisconsin "Manitowoc, Wisconsin").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)_Dione_'s keel was [laid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") on 10 November 1933,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 37–38  and her [contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract "Contract") was entered the same day for a price of [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")242,800.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:26-14): 318  The [launch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") of the cutters and her two sister ships, _[Electra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS\_Potomac\_(AG-25) "USS Potomac (AG-25)")_ and _[Pandora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC\_Pandora "USCGC Pandora")_, was originally to occur on 23 June 1934; it was postponed one week for per an announcement by the chief government inspector and shipyard officials.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-16): 2 _Dione_ was finally launched alongside her sister ships[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-17): 9  on 30 June,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) each cutter leaving the ways in intervals of twenty minutes[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:38-18): 2  beginning at 1100. _Dione_ was christened by Unita Risch, president of Wisconsin Department of the [American Legion Auxiliary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Legion_Auxiliary "American Legion Auxiliary").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:39-19): 1 [Champagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champagne "Champagne"), rather than [sparkling water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbonated_water "Carbonated water"), was used to [christen the cutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism#Boats_and_ships "Baptism") for the first time in a ship's launching in Manitowoc since Prohibition; it was also the first time that three vessels of that size had been launched [broadside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadside_(naval) "Broadside (naval)") at one time.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:37-11): 4  Around 10,000 people attended the triple launching.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:38-18): 2 [[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:39-19): 1

The first of her sisters to be completed,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-20): 5 _Dione_ was delivered on 28 September[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:18-21): 434  and then undertook her [sea trials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_trial "Sea trial"). The cutter was proclaimed "satisfactory" at her trials[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-22): 3  and was [commissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning "Ship commissioning") on 5 October.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 37–38  She was named for [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(Titaness) "Dione (Titaness)"), a [Titaness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titans "Titans") and the mother of the goddess [Aphrodite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphrodite "Aphrodite") in [Greek mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology"). _Dione_ cost US$258,000 to construct.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) The cutter's building number[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 37 [[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-23): 2  and designation was P-13;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:26-14): 318 [[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-patrolboatefn-24) her [signal letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_call_sign "Maritime call sign") were NRGV.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-25): 90  She bore the prefix "USCGC," indicating that she was a "[United States Coast Guard Cutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard_Cutter "United States Coast Guard Cutter")".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-USCGHO1-26)

Design and specifications
-------------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USCGC_Dione&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Design and specifications")]

[![Image 10: A top-down view of several decks of Dione's interior](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/2a/Accommodation_plans_of_USCGC_Dione.png/250px-Accommodation_plans_of_USCGC_Dione.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Accommodation_plans_of_USCGC_Dione.png)

[General arrangement plans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blueprint "Blueprint") of a _Thetis_-class patrol boat. Depicted are the berth deck, main deck, and two layers of superstructure.

_Dione_ had a [length overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") of 165 feet (50 m),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) a [length between perpendiculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_between_perpendiculars "Length between perpendiculars") of 160 feet (49 m),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383  a maximum [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 25 ft 3 in (7.70 m),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) and a beam at [waterline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterline "Waterline") of 23 ft 9 in (7.24 m).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 38  When she was constructed in 1933, the cutter had a [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 7 ft 8 in (2 m). Her [displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)") was 337 [long tons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_ton "Long ton") (342 [tonnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne")) while fully loaded. She had a [complement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship%27s_company "Ship's company") of 5 officers and 39 men. Her hull was made of steel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)

[![Image 11: Crew on deck of a boat near a deck gun and other equipment](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/3-inch_23-caliber_gun_aboard_USS_SC-291.jpg/250px-3-inch_23-caliber_gun_aboard_USS_SC-291.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:3-inch_23-caliber_gun_aboard_USS_SC-291.jpg)

A 3"/23-caliber gun aboard a [submarine chaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_chaser "Submarine chaser") in the late 1910s.

The _Thetis_-class patrol boats had two decks: the [main deck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_deck "Main deck") and [berth deck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berth_deck "Berth deck"). The latter was subdivided into [compartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compartment_(ship) "Compartment (ship)") by six transverse watertight [bulkheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulkhead_(partition) "Bulkhead (partition)"). The forwardmost spaces were the chain locker and [bosun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boatswain "Boatswain")'s store,[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-bosunefn-27) which were situated in front of the shared [enlisted quarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barracks "Barracks").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383  Directly behind that were four [staterooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabin_(ship) "Cabin (ship)") for the cutter's five officers, followed by the [fuel tanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuel_tank "Fuel tank") with a fuel capacity of 7,700 [U.S. gallons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._gallon "U.S. gallon") (29,000[L](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litre "Litre")) of [diesel fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diesel_fuel "Diesel fuel"), that were subdivided by two bulkheads.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383 [[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 37–38  Behind the tanks was the engine room, followed by separate enlisted and officer [messrooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mess "Mess") in the aft. On the main deck was a two-layered [superstructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstructure "Superstructure"), which consisted of the deckhouse and [pilot house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_(nautical) "Bridge (nautical)"). The deckhouse—the bottom layer of the superstructure—held the cutter's [heads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_(watercraft) "Head (watercraft)"), the radio room, and the captain's quarters. Atop the deckhouse was the pilot house, an auxiliary [diesel generator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diesel_generator "Diesel generator"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383  three 18 in (46 cm) [searchlights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Searchlight "Searchlight"), and two 1 lb (0.45 kg) guns on either side of the pilot house. Mounted on the [bow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bow_(watercraft) "Bow (watercraft)") was a [3-inch/23-caliber gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3-inch/23-caliber_gun "3-inch/23-caliber gun") supplied by a [magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_magazine "Naval magazine") located in the [keel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel "Keel"). Behind the superstructure were two [funnels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funnel_(ship) "Funnel (ship)"). On both sides of the aft funnel was the cutter's boats, which consisted of 19 ft (5.8 m) [dories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dory_(boat) "Dory (boat)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383

The cutters were propelled by two [Winton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winton_Motor_Carriage_Company "Winton Motor Carriage Company")[6-cylinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6-cylinder "6-cylinder"), [4-stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four-stroke_engine "Four-stroke engine")[diesel engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diesel_engine "Diesel engine"). Each piston had a 14 in (36 cm) [bore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bore_(engine) "Bore (engine)") and 16 in (41 cm) [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke_(engine) "Stroke (engine)") that could produce 450 [rotations per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_per_minute "Revolutions per minute") and 670 [brake horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Brake_horsepower "Horsepower") (500 kW),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6): 382–383  for a total of 1,340 brake horsepower (1,000 kW). The engines turned two three-bladed [propellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propeller "Propeller"). The cutter had a maximum speed of 16 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (30[km/h](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilometres_per_hour "Kilometres per hour"); 18[mph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_per_hour "Miles per hour")), a maximum sustained speed of 14 knots (26 km/h; 16 mph), a cruising speed of 11 knots (20 km/h; 13 mph), and an economic speed of 6 knots (11 km/h; 6.9 mph). She had a range of 1,750 [statute miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute_mile "Statute mile") (2,820 km)[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-milesefn-28) while traveling at her maximum sustained speed, a range of 3,000 statute miles (4,800 km) while traveling at her cruising speed, and a range of 6,417 statute miles (10,327 km) while traveling at her economic speed.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)

Coast Guard service
-------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USCGC_Dione&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Coast Guard service")]

_Dione_ departed Manitowoc the same day she was commissioned—5 October 1934.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-29): 29  She passed through the [Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Lakes "Great Lakes") and docked in [Ogdensburg, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogdensburg,_New_York "Ogdensburg, New York") for repairs to her oil purifier on 15 October.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:8-30): 5  The cutter traveled up through the remainder of the river and through the [gulf of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_St._Lawrence "Gulf of St. Lawrence").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:36-31): 2 _Dione_ stopped in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") on 30 October to be outfitted with her weaponry,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-32): 22 [[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-weaponsefn-33) and docked at the Coast Guard base on the [Elizabeth River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_River_(Virginia) "Elizabeth River (Virginia)") on 1 November in order to take on fuel and provisions.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:19-34): 16

_Dione_ was stationed in [Norfolk, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk,_Virginia "Norfolk, Virginia").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:2-35): 102  The cutter primarily operated in a [search and rescue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_and_rescue "Search and rescue") capacity, responding to vessels that had signaled that they were in distress,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-36): 6 [[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-37): 6  taking injured seamen to Norfolk,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-38): 1 [[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-39): 6  and locating the wreckage of downed planes.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-40): 1, 7  She also operated in various miscellaneous capacities, such as breaking through ice to allow ships access to the [Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith_Island,_Maryland "Smith Island, Maryland") and [Tangier Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangier,_Virginia#Geography "Tangier, Virginia") in February 1936[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-41): 6  and accompanying vessels participating in a [Hampton One-Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampton_One-Design "Hampton One-Design") race in August 1941.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-42): 18  In November 1937, _Dione_ joined the search for survivors of the sunken cargo ship [_Tzenny Chandris_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Tzenny_Chandris "SS Tzenny Chandris"), which had sunk in a storm off [Hatteras, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatteras,_North_Carolina "Hatteras, North Carolina"), on the night of 12–13 November. Multiple lifeboats were found empty, but 15 survivors were eventually found clinging to wreckage by the cutter [_Mendota_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Culver "HMS Culver") and were subsequently taken to Norfolk.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-43): 1 [[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-44)

Following the beginning of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-wwiiefn-45)_Dione_ was assigned to both the [Fifth Naval District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_naval_districts#Fifth_Naval_District "United States naval districts")—which contained the waters off [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") and [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina")[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:5-46)—and the [Eastern Sea Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Sea_Frontier "Eastern Sea Frontier"), a Navy operational command.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) She was based out of [Naval Operating Base Norfolk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Station_Norfolk#History "Naval Station Norfolk"). _Dione_ was assigned to [patrol duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_patrol "Maritime patrol") of the waters between Norfolk and [Morehead City, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morehead_City,_North_Carolina "Morehead City, North Carolina"), covering the [shipping lanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_lane "Sea lane") that passed by the [Outer Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Banks "Outer Banks") of North Carolina and going as far out as the [Gulf Stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Stream "Gulf Stream"). She also traveled to the [lightships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightship "Lightship") that operated off the Outer Banks to deliver and receive [mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mail "Mail").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 25  On 1 November 1941, President [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") signed [Executive Order 8929](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Executive_Order_8929&action=edit&redlink=1 "Executive Order 8929 (page does not exist)"),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-47) which transferred control of the Coast Guard from the Department of the Treasury to the Navy “for the duration of the emergency.”[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:24-48): 16  Sometime in 1941,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-rearmamentefn-3) the cutter's two 1 lb (0.45 kg) guns were removed. Installed were two racks to hold [depth charges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") and a [Y-gun depth charge launcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y-gun "Y-gun"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) which was designed to throw depth charges over the sides of the cutter and into the water.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-49): 3

[![Image 12: A map showing the shoreline of Virginia and North Carolina](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/d/d1/Fifth_Naval_District_map.jpg/250px-Fifth_Naval_District_map.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fifth_Naval_District_map.jpg)

This map shows the [waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast#Coastal_waters "Coast") of the Fifth Naval District off North Carolina and Virginia which _Dione_ patrolled during the Second Happy Time

The waters off the Outer Banks of North Carolina are nicknamed the "[Graveyard of the Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graveyard_of_the_Atlantic "Graveyard of the Atlantic")" due to the high amount of ships lost at sea off the coast. The [sandbars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoal "Shoal") shift due to rough waves and unpredictable weather.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 25  During World War II, this region also earned the additional nickname "[Torpedo Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_Alley "Torpedo Alley")" (alternatively Torpedo Junction[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:32-50): 24 ) due to the high number of U-boats patrolling off the Outer Banks. During the time period that lasted from January to June 1942 and was referred to as the "[Second Happy Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Happy_Time "Second Happy Time")" by _[Kriegsmarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriegsmarine "Kriegsmarine")_ officers as well as [Karl Dönitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_D%C3%B6nitz "Karl Dönitz")—[Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiral_(Germany) "Admiral (Germany)") of the _Kriegsmarine_ and in charge of U-boats,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-51) 397 [Allied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") ships were sunk by U-boats.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:5-46)[Adolphus Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolphus_Andrews "Adolphus Andrews"), the [rear admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_admiral_(United_States) "Rear admiral (United States)")[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-52) in charge of the Eastern Sea Frontier, compiled a group of twenty ships to help defend the [East Coast of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States "East Coast of the United States"). This consisted of _Dione_, six _Active_-class patrol boats, four 110-foot (34 m) [cruiser submarines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruiser_submarine "Cruiser submarine") built before World War I, three [_Eagle_-class subchasers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle-class_patrol_craft "Eagle-class patrol craft"), two [gunboats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunboat "Gunboat") from 1905, and four large [yachts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yacht "Yacht") that had been converted for military service.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:11-53): 176 [[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:20-54): 461–462  In addition to being the fastest vessel of the fleet,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:11-53): 176 _Dione_ was the only one that was large and capable enough of opposing the U-boats that operated in Torpedo Alley.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 25 [[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:2-35): 102

_Dione_ was under the command of [Lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_(navy) "Lieutenant (navy)") Nelson McCormick at the start of the Second Happy Time in January 1942. McCormick came to the conclusion that _Dione_ was too far away from ships, when they issued distress signals, to be able to assist them. Thus, he ordered his crew to conduct more aggressive and offensive patrols. After determining that U-boats generally attacked at night, McCormick decided to abandon his usual routine in favor of grid-searching the waters off the Outer Banks for U-boats;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 27 [[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:15-55): 28  these would utilize a World War I-era [sonar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonar "Sonar") system[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:32-50): 24  and other types of [sound-detection gear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_recognition "Sound recognition").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 27 [[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:15-55): 28

[![Image 13: Water is churned up behind the cutter as she moves forward](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Dione_depth_charges.png/250px-Dione_depth_charges.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dione_depth_charges.png)

_Dione_ deploying depth charges, 1942

Sometime at the end of January, _Dione_ dropped six depth charges after her sonar operator reported an "underwater object" 20 miles (32 km) off [Oregon Inlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Inlet "Oregon Inlet"). Two airplanes made several runs on a rapidly spreading patch of oil. They reported to McCormick that they saw something long and narrow. An oar and a boat hook eventually surfaced from the object, and when brought aboard were found to have been from the shipwreck of the [oil tanker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_tanker "Oil tanker")[_Francis E. Powell_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Francis_E._Powell "SS Francis E. Powell"); the tanker had been sunk by [_U-130_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-130_(1941) "German submarine U-130 (1941)") on 27 January.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 27–28  In early February, _Dione_ was ordered to [Little Creek Section Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Expeditionary_Base%E2%80%93Little_Creek#World_War_II "Joint Expeditionary Base–Little Creek") to pick up a new master, Lieutenant James Alger. McCormick was kept aboard _Dione_ as an executive officer, and to command the cutter when intricate maneuvers were required. On Alger's first day, _Dione_'s sonar operator called out two echoes; the second resulted in Alger giving an order to drop depth charges. Two life rafts were dispatched to collect samples of oil that bubbled to the surface. It was then discovered that _Dione_ had dropped depth charges on a sunken oil tanker.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 28, 33  On 12 February, the cutter's sonar operator reported a [periscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periscope "Periscope") off _Dione_'s [port side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_and_starboard "Port and starboard"). Alger ordered [general quarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_quarters "General quarters") and had depth charges dropped from both the Y-gun and the racks; some went off at 100 feet (30 m) while others went off at 50 feet (15 m). _Dione_'s lights and equipment abruptly went dead after her propellers came out of the water. The cutter's engines were stopped, and her electrical power was later restored. No U-boat was ever spotted.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 41

Later that month, on 19 February, the cutter towed the [minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper")[USS _Paramount_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Paramount "USS Paramount") to Morehead City after she had been grounded at the entrance to [Ocracoke Inlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocracoke_Inlet "Ocracoke Inlet").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 46 [[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-56)_Dione_ set off for [Cape Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Henry "Cape Henry") late at night on 27 February to assist the torpedoed [freighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cargo_ship "Cargo ship")_North Sea_. The freighter was found by _Dione_ early the next morning. Reportedly, a U-boat's attack on _North Sea_ had been halted due to a storm that had tossed the U-boat about, preventing it from accurately aiming its [deck gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deck_gun "Deck gun") and shelling the freighter. _Dione_ towed the damaged freighter to [Little Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Expeditionary_Base%E2%80%93Little_Creek#World_War_II "Joint Expeditionary Base–Little Creek"), as _North Sea_ had lost her steering capabilities in the attack, and arrived by the end of the day.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 50  Sometime in February 1942, the _Thetis_ class patrol boats were issued alpha-numeric designations, that began with WPC[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8): 166 [[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:24-48): 18 —PC stood for [patrol craft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrol_boat "Patrol boat"), and the W marked that it was part of the Coast Guard.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-USCGHO1-26)_Dione_ was issued the designation WPC-107.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:24-48): 18

[![Image 14: Crewmen peer over the side of Dione to pick up survivors of a shipwreck](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Dione_rescue.png/250px-Dione_rescue.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dione_rescue.png)

_Dione_'s crew rescuing that of a torpedoed ship, 1942

On 15 March, _Dione_ received a distress signal from the oil tanker _Australia_. The tanker had been torpedoed by [_U-332_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-332 "German submarine U-332") about 20 miles (32 km) away from the cutter. _Dione_ spotted _Australia_ a little after an hour, and the cutter's sonar operator had picked up an echo from the U-boat within two. _Dione_ launched depth charges but had no success.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-57): 79–80 _Dione_ rescued the crew of the storage tanker [_Acme_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Abarenda_(IX-131) "USS Abarenda (IX-131)") early in the morning of 18 March.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:31-58): 170  The tanker had been torpedoed by [_U-124_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-124_(1940) "German submarine U-124 (1940)") one [nautical mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (1.9 km; 1.2 mi) west of the [Diamond Shoals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_Shoals "Diamond Shoals") Light Buoy just before midnight the previous day.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-59) The cutter also picked up the survivors of the Greek freighter [_Kassandra Louloudis_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Kassandra_Louloudis "SS Kassandra Louloudis"), which had been torpedoed by the same U-boat that attacked _Acme_ just after midnight on 18 March.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:31-58): 170  The cutter took the survivors of both ships to Norfolk.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-60) On 20 March, _Dione_ made contact with a U-boat. A Coast Guard airplane from the [Elizabeth City Air Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_Guard_Air_Station_Elizabeth_City "Coast Guard Air Station Elizabeth City") dropped two depth charges.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) On 23 March, she responded to the distress signals of the oil tanker _[Naeco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS\_Naeco "SS Naeco")_, torpedoed by _U-124_. The cutter rescued at least ten survivors from a lifeboat and two more from the water, all of whom were taken to Norfolk.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 96–98 [[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:22-61) Three days later, on 26 March, the crew of _Dione_ spotted flames from the oil tanker [_Dixie Arrow_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Dixie_Arrow "SS Dixie Arrow") and traveled several miles to investigate. The tanker's survivors had already been rescued by the destroyer [USS _Tarbell_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Tarbell "USS Tarbell"), and the cutter encountered nothing but debris. _Dione_ then headed south to the waters off Hatteras, North Carolina.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 102  On 5 April, the cutter responded to the torpedoed oil tanker [_Byron D. Benson_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Byron_D._Benson "SS Byron D. Benson"), and pulled one survivor from the water.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 123 [[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) On 7 April, [_U-552_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-552 "German submarine U-552") torpedoed the oil tanker [_British Splendour_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_British_Splendour "MV British Splendour").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-62)_Dione_ dropped depth charges on the U-boat which reportedly almost hit,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-63): 7 [[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:33-64): 129  though _U-552_ managed to escape.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:33-64): 129

[![Image 15: An oil tanker is half-visible just behind the stern of Dione; the tanker is partially cut out by the camera's frame](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a7/Dione_escort.jpg/250px-Dione_escort.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dione_escort.jpg)

_Dione_ escorting a convoy, 1942; her Y-gun can be seen behind the sailor in the foreground

_Dione_ rendezvoused with the destroyer [USS _Dickerson_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Dickerson "USS Dickerson") on 14 April, near the Diamond Shoals Light Buoy, to escort a [convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Allied_convoys_during_World_War_II_by_region#North_American_coastal_and_Caribbean_convoys "List of Allied convoys during World War II by region"). Lieutenant Dick Bacchus had taken over as the cutter's navigator and executive officer, arriving on 11 April from [USCGC _Modoc_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Modoc "USCGC Modoc"); Alger remained aboard as the commander. The convoy was later joined by another cutter, and escorted two freighters north past North Carolina. After _Dickerson_ relieved both cutters of duty, _Dione_ headed back south for a nightly patrol. At morning on 15 April, the cutter met up with _Dickerson_ once more to escort a convoy, this time consisting of two British trawlers, two American tankers, and an American freighter. The tankers were quicker than the cutter, and she had issues keeping up. Alger chose to be aggressive despite the fact that the cutter was supposed to remain close by the convoy, ranging out and dropping depth charges on any suspected echoes to "keep the U-boat[s] off balance."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 164–166  For the next few days, _Dione_ escorted convoys during the day and patrolled the waters for U-boats during the night. The convoys were nicknamed "[bucket brigades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bucket_brigade "Bucket brigade")" after the old-fashioned method of transporting buckets during a fire.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 167  These convoys traveled during the day and then docked in ports overnight; this was possible on the East Coast due to its abundance of good harbors.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-65): 132–133, 254–256  No ships were lost to U-boats near [Cape Hatteras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Hatteras "Cape Hatteras") or [Cape Lookout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Lookout_(North_Carolina) "Cape Lookout (North Carolina)") after the establishment of the "bucket brigade" convoy system.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 167  On 18 April, _Dione_ was observed dropping depth charges on a U-boat, with no visible results.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)

On 19 April, _Dione_ led a convoy of nine civilian vessels alongside another 88-foot cutter. The convoy passed Cape Hatteras without incident. A Navy aircraft spotted an incoming torpedo; Alger ordered evasive maneuvers. The torpedo missed _Dione_ by about 20 yards but struck the oil tanker _Axtell J. Byles_ at 2000 hours, which sank some time thereafter. _Dione_ dropped eight depth charges over the course of two runs in response to the attack.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 167–170  The convoys began to run at night following the loss of _Axtell J. Byles_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 178 _Dione_ began patrolling around the [Wimble Shoals](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wimble_Shoals&action=edit&redlink=1 "Wimble Shoals (page does not exist)") Buoy after her escort missions were finished, beginning demolition exercises on the wreck of _Axtell J. Byles_ on April 25. She would continue dropping depth charges for the next few days.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 178  On 29 April, _Dione_ was ordered back to Little Creek for repairs and rearmament.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-rearmamentefn-3)

The repairs to _Dione_ were finished on 13 May.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 178, 231  Leaving Little Creek, she was accompanied by a writer and [photographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photojournalism "Photojournalism") from _[The Saturday Evening Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Saturday\_Evening\_Post "The Saturday Evening Post")_. The cutter escorted two ships and afterwards dropped depth charges on an unknown sonar ping that the writer from _The Saturday Evening Post_ had called "Wimble Willy."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 231–232  The photographs were published in a 1942 article.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)

[![Image 16: The ships sail across the ocean in convoy](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Convoy_in_WWII_off_North_Carolina.jpg/250px-Convoy_in_WWII_off_North_Carolina.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Convoy_in_WWII_off_North_Carolina.jpg)

A convoy off the coast of North Carolina sometime during World War II. _Dione_ escorted similar convoys during the latter half of the Second Happy Time

On 18 May, _Dione_ left Norfolk to join a convoy heading to [Key West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_West "Key West"), [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"). On 20 May, it was discovered that the cutter's port engine was "acting up". It was decided that she would continue on the convoy running on one engine while her other one was repaired. _Dione_ traveled in the starboard quarter of the convoy and occasionally traveled further away from the convoy to listen for sonar pings. The cutter was eventually forced to fall to the rear position after a ship began lagging behind. The convoy reached Florida on 23 May.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 233–235  Sometime in May, _Dione_ met up with the destroyer [USS _Ellis_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Ellis_(DD-154) "USS Ellis (DD-154)"). The two vessels completed support missions and responded to Coast Guard aircraft reports, steaming to the location of two allegedly damaged and submerged U-boats roughly 50 miles (80 km) off the coast of [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") and dropping depth charges on them.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:2-35): 102

On 15 June, a convoy _Dione_ was escorting formed a single-file line in preparation to enter the [Chesapeake Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay "Chesapeake Bay"). The fifth oil tanker in line, _Robert C. Tuttle_, struck a [mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_mine "Naval mine") and began to sink within view of vacationers in [Virginia Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Beach,_Virginia "Virginia Beach, Virginia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 254–255  The oil tanker _Esso Augusta_ broke the formation as her crew believed that _Robert C. Tuttle_ had been torpedoed by a U-boat, and _Esso Augusta_ ended up striking a second mine as a result. _Dione_ dropped a spread of eight depth charges, and her ninth caused another explosion to occur. Eyewitnesses claimed to have seen a U-boat, but naval officials concluded that the incident was due to mines laid in the [Thimble Shoal Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thimble_Shoal_Channel&action=edit&redlink=1 "Thimble Shoal Channel (page does not exist)") between Virginia Beach and [Virginia's eastern shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Shore_of_Virginia "Eastern Shore of Virginia").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-66) On 24 June, at 1900 hours, the cutter made an underwater contact[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) while escorting a northbound convoy of eleven ships.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:20-54): 607  Five minutes later, _Dione_ dropped one depth charge with no results. After sunset,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:20-54): 607  at 1910 hours,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) two other ships in the convoy, _Nordland_ and _Manuela_, were torpedoed[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) by [_U-404_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-404 "German submarine U-404").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:20-54): 607 _Dione_ made a sweeping search for the U-boat, which seemed to be on the starboard side of the convoy. _Nordland_ caught fire and sink, and her survivors were rescued by _Norwich City_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)_U-404_ attempted a second attack, but was stopped before it could do so by _Dione_ and an aircraft.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:20-54): 607

_Dione_ made an underwater contact the next day, 25 June, dropping five depth charges. Large amounts of oil bubbled to the surface. A doubtful contact was made just two days later, on 27 June, at 1054 hours. The cutter dropped four depth charges but yielded no results.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)_Dione_ was taken to Norfolk for repairs to her starboard engine at the end of the month. They lasted a week, and the cutter was back into action at the beginning of July.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 313, 321  She continued her convoy escort duties into July and August,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 322  though the U-boat threat off the Outer Banks had become non-existent by then.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 322–325  Following the [end of the Second Happy Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Happy_Time#US_convoys_arrive "Second Happy Time"), the crew of _Dione_ began to refer to the period as the "Battle of Torpedo Junction."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:1-1): 19

#### September 1942–1944

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USCGC_Dione&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: September 1942–1944")]

_Dione_ was listed as a convoy escort unit[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:34-67): 119  and conducted escort duty in the [North Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean#North_Atlantic "Atlantic Ocean"),[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-68): 3  escorting HK convoys going from New York to Key West[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-69): 122  and KN convoys heading from Key West to New York. She was based out of [Tompkinsville, Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tompkinsville,_Staten_Island "Tompkinsville, Staten Island") from December 1943[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:34-67): 49  to December 1944;[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:35-70): 53  Thompkinsville was the site of an Eastern Sea Frontier Base.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-71)

[![Image 17: A submarine is in the foreground; to its right are two ships. Dione is to the left, and a smaller unknown ship is to the right](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/German_submarine_U-1228_surrenders_at_Portsmouth_NH_in_May_1945.jpg/250px-German_submarine_U-1228_surrenders_at_Portsmouth_NH_in_May_1945.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:German_submarine_U-1228_surrenders_at_Portsmouth_NH_in_May_1945.jpg)

_Dione_ (center) escorts _U-1228_ to Portsmouth, New Hampshire, on 17 May 1945

In 1945, _Dione_ underwent a major refit. Her 3-inch/23-caliber gun was removed. In addition to her Y-gun and two depth charge racks, the cutter was fitted with two single-mount [3-inch/50-caliber guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3-inch/50-caliber_gun "3-inch/50-caliber gun"), two single-mount [20 mm/80 cannons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon"), two ["Mousetrap" anti-submarine rocket launchers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mousetrap_(weapon) "Mousetrap (weapon)"), and an additional Y-gun. Her wireless set and World War I-era sonar system was replaced with an SF [radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radar "Radar") system and a QCN-1 sonar system.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 37–38 _Dione_'s displacement was increased to 350 long tons (360 t) and her draft was increased to 10 feet (3 m). Her complement was also increased to 7 officers and 68 men.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)

The cutter was selected as one of six patrol vessels to serve as the Navy's "Surrender Group" for the [First Naval District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_naval_districts#First_Naval_District "United States naval districts") off [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England"), and served alongside her sister ships [_Argo_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Argo "USCGC Argo") and _Nemesis_. The role of the Surrender Group was to help escort surrendered [Axis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") vessels to American ports, where they would then be acquired by the [United States government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States"). Dönitz, now serving as [President of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Germany_(1919%E2%80%931945) "President of Germany (1919–1945)") following the death of [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler"), had broadcast an order for all U-boats to surrender to Allied ports in early May.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-72)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-73): 18  On 17 May, _Dione_ rendezvoused with [_U-1228_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-1228 "German submarine U-1228"), a U-boat that had fled to Allied waters following the German surrender.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:27-74) It had received its surrender orders on 9 May and was instructed to head to [St. John's, Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John%27s,_Newfoundland_and_Labrador "St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador"). The U-boat bypassed St. John's due to poor conditions and headed to a new surrender point at [Casco Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casco_Bay "Casco Bay"). _U-1228_ was escorted to [Portsmouth, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth,_New_Hampshire "Portsmouth, New Hampshire") by [USS _Neal A. Scott_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Neal_A._Scott "USS Neal A. Scott"), arriving at 0600 hours on 17 May.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-75)_Dione_ escorted the U-boat into Portsmouth later that day.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:27-74)_Dione_ was sent back to the Fifth Naval District in June, where she was assigned to [air-sea rescue duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-sea_rescue "Air-sea rescue").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)

On 1 January 1946, jurisdiction of the Coast Guard was given back to the Department of the Treasury via [Executive Order 9666](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Executive_Order_9666&action=edit&redlink=1 "Executive Order 9666 (page does not exist)"), signed by President [Harry S. Truman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman "Harry S. Truman").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:24-48): 21 [[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-76) From 1945 to 1947, _Dione_ was used by the Coast Guard for [law enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_enforcement "Law enforcement") and search and rescue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) She was eventually [decommissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning#Ship_decommissioning "Ship commissioning") on 23 July 1947, in [Cape May, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_May,_New_Jersey "Cape May, New Jersey"),[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:12-77): 185  where she spent several years [laid up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_fleet "Reserve fleet")[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:25-78): 261  in storage due to a lack of personnel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) The cutter was recommissioned on 4 February 1951, in [Curtis Bay, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis_Bay,_Baltimore "Curtis Bay, Baltimore"),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:9-79): 9–10  after a [shakedown cruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakedown_cruise "Shakedown cruise") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean"). Starting in 1952, _Dione_ was assigned to the [Eighth Coast Guard District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard#Districts_and_units "United States Coast Guard") and based in [Freeport, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeport,_Texas "Freeport, Texas");[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:13-80): 150  she was the first cutter to be based in the city.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:12-77): 185  Reportedly, Freeport competed with the city of [Corpus Christi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_Christi,_Texas "Corpus Christi, Texas") to be the location where _Dione_ was stationed.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:17-81): 2  The cutter was originally scheduled to arrive on 13 March 1952 but was delayed until 19 March due to rough weather on her shakedown cruise.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-82): 1  She was met with a yacht escort upon her arrival in Freeport that day. Local schools were closed so students could visit _Dione,_ and an enlisted men's dance and officer's dinner was held.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:12-77): 185 [[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:9-79): 9–10  The day was officially proclaimed "Coast Guard Day" by the cities of Freeport, [Velasco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velasco,_Texas "Velasco, Texas"), [Clute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clute,_Texas "Clute, Texas"), and [Lake Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Jackson,_Texas "Lake Jackson, Texas").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:12-77): 185 _Dione_ was located at the Freeport Lifeboat Station.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:12-77): 185 [[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:17-81): 2

_Dione_ operated in a similar capacity as she had in Norfolk, that being search and rescue and law enforcement.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-83): 212  Among many other incidents, the cutter responded to the distress signal of a Mexican motor vessel in 1956,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-84): 5  towed the disabled [USCGC _Iris_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Iris "USCGC Iris") in 1957,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-85): 4  helped put out a fire that had started aboard the Freeport sulfur [barge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barge "Barge")_FS-20_ in 1959,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-86): 6  and towed a fishing vessel after a false emergency signal in 1962.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-87): 5  In 1953, per international rules, the cutter was required to install a forward masthead light 16 feet (4.9 m) above the hull, and install an after range light—the horizontal distance had to be 18 feet (5.5 m).[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-88): 16  She was also the first of five 165 feet (50 m)-long[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-165fn-89) cutters to undergo repairs to her hull in 1960. It was discovered that her insides had [corroded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrosion "Corrosion") and were hidden by insulation and furniture and her C [strake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strake "Strake")[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-strakefn-91) had several leaks; attempts to use [welding arcs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arc_welding "Arc welding") to fix the latter ended up "burning through the basic plate" and resulted in _Dione_'s entire strake needing to be replaced. As a result of the experience with _Dione_, a routine was established to inspect the hulls of the remainder of the cutters.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-92): 17

_Dione_ remained in Freeport until 1963, when she was set to be decommissioned.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) A farewell party was held for the crew on 31 January.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-93): 11 _Dione_ left Freeport on 2 February.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:30-94): 12–13  She arrived in [Levingston Shipyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levingston_Shipbuilding_Company "Levingston Shipbuilding Company") in [Orange, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange,_Texas "Orange, Texas"), on 4 February.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:30-94): 20–21  The cutter was decommissioned on 8 February,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) and her custody was transferred to the Texas Group of the [Atlantic Reserve Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_reserve_fleets#Atlantic_Reserve_Fleet "United States Navy reserve fleets")—the [Atlantic Reserve Fleet, Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Station_Orange#Atlantic_Reserve_Fleet,_Orange "United States Naval Station Orange")—that same day.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:30-94): 29 _Dione_ was sold as a [supply ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auxiliary_ship "Auxiliary ship") on 24 February 1964.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:10-15): 37

After being sold, _Dione_ became a [merchant ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merchant_ship "Merchant ship"), carrying the [official number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_number#U.S._official_number "Official number") 297193[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:16-97): 233 [[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:21-98): 63  and the call sign WD4627.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:21-98): 63 [[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:14-99): 180  She was first owned by the Palmer Decker Boat Company and registered in [Port Arthur, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Arthur,_Texas "Port Arthur, Texas"), according to the 1965 edition of _[Merchant Vessels of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Merchant\_Vessels\_of\_the\_United\_States&action=edit&redlink=1 "Merchant Vessels of the United States (page does not exist)")_ which had been created during 1964.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:14-99): 180  In March 1967, the Palmer Decker Boat Company was dissolved following a [liquidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquidation "Liquidation") agreement unanimously executed by the company's [shareholders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shareholder "Shareholder").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-100): 15  The ship was seized by a [US Marshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marshals_Service "United States Marshals Service") in September 1967 after [foreclosure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreclosure "Foreclosure") proceedings were filed against the Palmer Decker Boat Company by the Associates Discount Corporation in case 67–1335.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-101): 54  The [United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_Eastern_District_of_Louisiana "United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana") ruled in November that "_Dione_, her engines, tackle, apparel, etc." should be [sold at a court auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_auction "Court auction") to the highest bidder on 7 December.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-102): 53

In the 1969 edition of _Merchant Vessels of the United States_, created during 1968, the ship is listed under the name _Big Trouble_, the ownership of Big Trouble Inc., and is registered in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-103): 99  Big Trouble was renamed to Delta Boats Inc. in February 1969,[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-104)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-105): 15  and _Big Trouble_ was [conveyed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conveyancing "Conveyancing") to Delta Boats.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-106): 16  In March 1969, under the name _Delta I_,[[k]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-efndelta-96) she was sold from Delta Boats to Sabik Inc.,[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-107): 165  still registered in New Orleans.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:16-97): 233

On 5 April 1969, listed as a [geophysical exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exploration_geophysics "Exploration geophysics") ship, _Delta I_ caught fire while going from [Kingston, Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Jamaica "Kingston, Jamaica"), to [Port of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Spain "Port of Spain"), the capital city of [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago"); she was bound for the [Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"). She had left the United States on 25 March. The crew of _Delta I_ had failed to extinguish an engine fire and abandoned the ship in her lifeboats. An [SOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOS "SOS") was received by the American [Guantanamo Bay Naval Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_Naval_Base "Guantanamo Bay Naval Base") in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"), which subsequently dispatched search planes. After locating the ship, the planes messaged Kingston for a [Jamaican Defense Force Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Defence_Force#JDF_Coast_Guard "Jamaica Defence Force") patrol boat. The crew were rescued by the Jamaican Defense Force Coast Guard and a [salvage vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvage_tug "Salvage tug") was sent to put out the blaze and recover the ship.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-108): 19 _Delta I_ was almost completely gutted by the time the fire was extinguished, with only her hull [salvageable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_salvage "Marine salvage") when she was towed to [Tampa, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa,_Florida "Tampa, Florida").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:232-109): 9

The ship was overhauled for almost a year,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:232-109): 9  briefly seized by a US Marshal in February 1970 in pursuant of an [arrest warrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_arrest "Ship arrest") filed by the Crownwell Corporation[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-110): 34 —an [oil well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_well "Oil well") servicing company whose majority interest had been acquired by private investors in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") in January[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-111): 161 —and _Delta I_ was refitted by March that year as a "[jack-of-all trades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_of_all_trades "Jack of all trades")" ship. She was capable of serving as "an [oil rig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_platform "Oil platform") tender, a crew boat, [buoy tender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buoy_tender "Buoy tender"), repair ship with [sand blast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandblasting "Sandblasting") capacity, and a line-handling vessel for [super tankers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_tanker "Oil tanker")." The ship was still owned by Sabik despite the seizure, and she was chartered to the Mideast Trading Company.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:232-109): 9  In late 1969, the name of the ship was changed to _Al Rashid._[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-112): 155 [[j]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-efnnamechange-95)

_Al Rashid_ carried the [IMO number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMO_number "IMO number") 7515080 and was listed as a supply ship in the 1978–1979 edition of _[Lloyd's Register of Shipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s\_Register#The\_Register "Lloyd's Register")_.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:6-113): 104  She had a length of 154.3 feet (47 m), a beam of 25.3 feet (7.7 m), and a draft of 11.3 feet (3.4 m). She had a [gross register tonnage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_register_tonnage "Gross register tonnage") of 256 and a [net register tonnage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_register_tonnage "Net register tonnage") of 174.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:21-98): 63 [[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:7-114): 37

The fate of the former _Dione_ is unknown, though she was last seen in service in 1992 as _Al Rashid_.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:25-78): 261
