[Warship Wednesday, Aug. 15, 2018: Florida’s ancient sub-buster](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/)

_Here at LSOZI, we are going to take off every [Wednesday for a look at the old steam/diesel navies of the 1859-1946 period](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/category/warship-wednesday/) and will profile a different ship each week. These ships have a life, a tale all their own, which sometimes takes them to the strangest places. – Christopher Eger_

**Warship Wednesday, Aug. 15, 2018: Florida’s ancient sub-buster**

[![Image 127: Woman wearing a skirt suit stands on a pier with a boat behind her](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/gasparilla-festival-attendee-tampa-1953-atlanta-journal-constitution-photographs-coast-guard-cutter-nemesis-in-background.jpg?resize=519%2C628&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/gasparilla-festival-attendee-tampa-1953-atlanta-journal-constitution-photographs-coast-guard-cutter-nemesis-in-background/)

_Atlanta Journal-Constitution Photograph_

Here we see, behind the striking young lady, is the _Argo_-class 165-foot (B) submarine chaser/cutter _Nemesis (WPC-111)_ of the U.S. Coast Guard, taken during the 1953 Gasparilla Festival in Tampa. _Nemesis_ was just under 20 at the time and had an interesting life both prior to and after this image was snapped.

The USCG’s two-dozen 165-footers were built during the early-1930s and they proved successful in WWII, with two sinking U-boats. Based on the earlier _USCGC Tallapoosa (WPG-52)_, the 165-foot class of cutters was divided into two groups, the first designed primarily for derelict destruction and SAR, the second for Prohibition bootlegger busting:

The first batch, the six Class A vessels, were named after Native American tribes– _Algonquin, Comanche, Escanaba, Mohawk, Onondaga,_ and _Tahoma_— and had a 36-foot beam, a 13.5-foot maximum draft, a sedate speed of 13 knots, and a displacement of 1,005 tons. We’ve covered a couple of this class of “beefy” 165s before to include [USCGC Mohawk](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/tag/uscgc-mohawk/) and cannot talk these hardy boats up enough. Tragically, one of these, _USCGC Escanaba (WPG-77)_, was lost after encountering a U-boat or mine in 1943 with only two survivors.

[![Image 128: U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Modoc from 1922-1947](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/cgc-165-cutter-modoc-sm.jpg?resize=519%2C278&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/cgc-165-cutter-modoc-sm/)

_The more beefy 165-foot (A) class cutters (Coast Guard Collection)_

The follow-on 18 WPCs in Class B were named after Greek mythos– _Argo, Ariadne, Atalanta, Aurora, Calypso, Cyane, Daphne, Dione, Galatea, Hermes, Icarus, Nemesis, Nike, Pandora, Perseus, Thetis, Triton,_ and _Electra_. They were much lighter at 337-tons, narrower with a 25-foot beam, could float in under 10-feet of water (the designed draft was ~7ft.) and, on their suite of direct reversible GM-made Winton diesels, could touch 16 knots while keeping open the possibility of a 6,400nm range if poking around at a much lower speed.

[![Image 129: U.S. Coast Guard Cutter ICARUS 1932-1946 in 1942 configuration is shown in a technical drawing from the ship's port side](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/coast-guard-cutter-icarus-drawn-in-profile-coast-guard-collection-165-sm.jpg?resize=519%2C272&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/coast-guard-cutter-icarus-drawn-in-profile-coast-guard-collection-165-sm/)

_Coast Guard Cutter Icarus, an example of the 165 (B)s, drawn in profile. Note the short, twin stacks. (Coast Guard Collection)_

They were built between 1931 and 1934 at a series of five small commercial yards and were designed as patrol vessels. Their normal armament consisted of a dated 3-inch/23 caliber Mk 7 gun and two 37mm Mk. 4 1-pounders. Due to their designed role in busting up Rum Row, their small arms locker included a few Thompson M1921 sub guns, M1911s and a number of Springfield 1903s for good measure.

[![Image 130: Three U.S. Coast Guard Grumman JRF Goose planes fly above a U.S. Coast Guard cutter in a vintage black and white photograph](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/coast-guard-planes-from-the-coast-guard-air-station-miami-florida-greeting-new-165-foot-patrol-boat-pandora-arrival-december-6-1934-e1534066499392.jpg?resize=519%2C355&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/coast-guard-planes-from-the-coast-guard-air-station-miami-florida-greeting-new-165-foot-patrol-boat-pandora-arrival-december-6-1934/)

_“Coast Guard planes from the Coast Guard Air Station Miami, Florida, greeting new 165-foot patrol boat PANDORA arrival December 6, 1934, to take station.” Top to bottom Flying Boat ACAMAR, Amphibian SIRIUS and Flying Boat A. As you note, the slimmer twin-funnel 165-foot (B) class sub chasers had a much different profile_

The subject of our tale, _Nemesis_ (can you get a better name for a warship?), was ordered for $258,000 from Marietta Manufacturing Co. at Point Pleasant, West Virginia, on the Ohio River, alongside her sisters _Nike_ and _Triton_, in 1931. All three commissioned the same day– 7 July 1934– ironically some six months after Prohibition ended.

_Nemesis_ and her 44-man crew (5 officers, 39 enlisted) set sail for St. Petersburg, Florida, where they would consider home for the rest of her (peacetime) career with the Coast Guard.

[![Image 131: Vintage U.S. Coast Guard Cutter NEMESIS envelope dated November 1934 is addressed to Robert Lucas in Woodside, L.I., N.Y., and bears postage stamps and a postmark from Trenton](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/uss-trenton-cover-welcoming-nemesis-to-ste-pte.jpg?resize=519%2C296&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/uss-trenton-cover-welcoming-nemesis-to-ste-pte/)

_USS Trenton postal cover welcoming Nemesis to Ste Pte_

With tensions ramping up prior to the U.S entry to WWII, several East Coast 165s, to include _Algonquin, Comanche, Galatea, Pandora, Thetis,_ and _Triton_, were on duty with the Navy after 1 July 1941 to assist with the Neutrality Patrol. The rest would follow immediately after Pearl Harbor. Armed with hastily-installed depth charge racks and a thrower and given a couple of Lewis guns for added muscle, they went looking for U-boats as the defenders of the Eastern Sea Frontier.

[![Image 132: A grayscale view of a warship sailing through the water](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/coast-guard-cutter-argo-on-patrol-displaying-world-war-ii-armament-and-haze-gray-paint-scheme-165-b-nemesis-sister.jpg?resize=519%2C328&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/coast-guard-cutter-argo-on-patrol-displaying-world-war-ii-armament-and-haze-gray-paint-scheme-165-b-nemesis-sister/)

_Nemesis’s sister, USCGC Argo on patrol displaying World War II armament and haze gray paint scheme. Note the 3″/50 forward._

As [noted by DANFS:](https://www.history.navy.mil/research/histories/ship-histories/danfs/n/nemesis.html)

> The Gulf Sea Frontier, which included the Florida and Gulf coasts and parts of the Bahamas and Cuba, was defended in only rudimentary fashion during the early months of the war. Initial defenses consisted of the three Coast Guard cutters Nemesis, Nike, and Vigilant, together with nineteen unarmed Coast Guard aircraft and fourteen lightly armed Army aircraft.
> 
> 
> In late February 1942 four ships were torpedoed in four days, and in May 41 vessels were sent to the bottom by hostile submarine action off the Florida coast and in the Gulf. As sinkings mounted alarmingly in the Gulf Sea Frontier waters, American defensive strength in the area began to increase rapidly and overwhelmingly.

Sister [_Icarus (WPC-110)_](https://uboat.net/allies/warships/ship/11102.html) in May 1942 depth-charged _U-352_, sinking the submarine off the North Carolina coast and taking aboard 33 of her survivors. [_Thetis (WPC-115)_](https://uboat.net/allies/warships/ship/11097.html) scratched _U-157_ north of Havana just a few weeks later. Meanwhile, at the same time, _Nike (WPC-112)_ attacked and “[likely sank](https://www.mypalmbeachpost.com/news/years-later-how-world-war-changed-florida-forever/1NSp5jL6pRb01HgbyHMz4H/)” a surfaced U-boat off Florida’s Jupiter lighthouse then [rescued 19](https://uboat.net/allies/merchants/ship/1727.html) from a torpedoed Panamanian freighter.

Operating in the 7th Naval District on coastal patrol and convoy escort duty throughout the conflict, _Nemesis_ rescued 28 from the Mexican tanker _Faja De Oro_, torpedoed by _U-106_ off Key West in May 1942, an attack that helped spark Mexico’s entry into the War against Germany.

[![Image 133: Summary of a ship rescuing 28 survivors from 2 lifeboats, on May 21, 1942](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/nemesis.jpg?resize=519%2C208&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/nemesis/)

[![Image 134: Recuerda el 13 de mayo de 1942 is a propaganda poster by the Secretaria de Educacion Publica with a veiled woman crying and a sinking ship in the background](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/remember-the-13th-of-may-referring-to-a-mexican-oil-tanker-sunk-off-the-coast-of-florida-by-a-german-submarine-mexico-wwii.jpg?resize=519%2C710&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/remember-the-13th-of-may-referring-to-a-mexican-oil-tanker-sunk-off-the-coast-of-florida-by-a-german-submarine-mexico-wwii/)

_“Remember the 13th of May”, referring to a Mexican oil tanker, Faja De Oro, sunk off the coast of Florida by a German submarine. Nemesis saved her crew. Mexico declared war on the Axis Powers in support of the Allies on 22 May and, along with Brazil, was the only Latin American country to send their sons to fight overseas during World War II– notably the flyers of Escuadrón 201 who took U.S.-supplied P-47s to the Philippines as part of the Fifth Air Force, flying 785 combat sorties._

The next month, _Nemesis_ again had to pluck men from the Florida Straits. This time 27 men from the American-flagged _SS Suwied_, sank by _U-107_ on her way from Mobile to British Guyana.

[![Image 135: The image shows the rescue of 27 survivors of the torpedoed SS Suwied, on June 7, 1942, by Cutter Nemesis](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/suwied.jpg?resize=519%2C207&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/suwied/)

Our cutter did not manage to bag a U-boat on her own, although she reported contacts on several occasions and dropped a spread several times. Between February and August 1942 she launched attacks on submarine contacts on at least **five** different occasions.

By 1944, _Nemesis_, like the rest of her class, had their armament replaced by two 3″/50 guns, two 20mm Oerlikons, 2 Mousetrap ASW throwers as well as more advanced depth charges and throwers. _Nemesis_ was also one of just five of her class that carried SF-1 radar and QCN-1 sonar, sensors that the humble 165s were never designed for.

In 1945, the Navy selected six patrol vessels as its “[Surrender Group](https://media.defense.gov/2017/Jun/26/2001768978/-1/-1/0/SEAHISTORY142%20ELIOTWINSLOW1.PDF)” in the 1st Naval District including the three up-armed 165-foot Coast Guard cutters– _Dione_, _Nemesis_, and _Argo_. These ships helped process the surrender of at least five German submarines, _U-234, U-805, U-873, U-1228,_ and _U-858_. Notably, _U-234_ was packed with sensitive cargo to include senior German officers and 1,200 pounds of uranium.

[![Image 136: Gray U-boat in open water, with a boat nearby](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/german-submarine-u-805-after-surrendering-to-the-u-s-navy-off-portsmouth-new-hampshire-on-16-may-1945-national-archives.jpg?resize=519%2C343&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/german-submarine-u-805-after-surrendering-to-the-u-s-navy-off-portsmouth-new-hampshire-on-16-may-1945-national-archives/)

_Kodachrome of German Submarine U-805 after surrendering to the U.S. Navy off Portsmouth, New Hampshire, on 16 May 1945. National Archives. Nemesis was part of the Navy’s “Surrender Group” handling these boats._

_Nemesis_ received one battle star for her World War II service and chopped back to the USCG in 1946.

Postwar, _Nemesis_ picked up her white scheme and, losing some of her depth charges, went back to St. Pete.

[![Image 137: U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Nemesis sailing in calm waters](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/nemesis-1950.jpg?resize=800%2C595&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/nemesis-1950/)

_Closer to her festival picture at the beginning of the post. Note the extensive awnings. South Fla gets warm about 10 months a year. Also, note the 3″/50_

By 1953, most of her class had been decommissioned with only _Ariadne, Aurora, Dione, Nemesis, Nike, Pandora, Perseus_ and _Triton_ still on active duty. On the East Coast, _Triton_ was stationed in Key West and _Nemesis_ was in St. Pete. _Nike_ was in Gulfport, MS.

Decommissioned after a busy 30-year career on 20 November 1964, _Nemesis_ was sold on 9 February 1966 in a public auction, going to Auto Marine Engineers of Miami who parted her out over the years. (One of her masts [could be](https://books.google.com/books?id=gdjlBQAAQBAJ&pg=PT246&lpg=PT246&dq=nemesis+Auto+Marine+Engineers&source=bl&ots=pLz9jHL-t2&sig=9ecpcOj16yNZTCRlcUZngIx09r4&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwi489n5oOfcAhUSWqwKHU3pD2IQ6AEwBnoECAQQAQ#v=onepage&q=nemesis%20Auto%20Marine%20Engineers&f=false) on the late PBS&J Corporation founder Howard Malvern “Budd” Post’s Waterside estate.)

Renamed _Livingston’s Landing_, her hulk was rebuilt by 1979 to look like a triple-decker African steamer and used as a floating restaurant in Ft. Lauderdale, picking up the name _[Ancient Mariner](http://www.iamlasolas.com/the-ancient-mariner-on-the-new-river/)_ in 1981 while performing the same job. She was docked just west of where Hyde Park Market used to be, across from jail.

[![Image 138: Boat restaurant, The Ancient Mariner, decorated with lights floating on water at night](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/ancient-mariner-floating-restaurant-in-ft-lauderdale-florida.jpg?resize=519%2C326&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/ancient-mariner-floating-restaurant-in-ft-lauderdale-florida/)

Sadly, “the floating eatery was closed in 1986 by health officials as the source of a massive outbreak of infectious hepatitis” that [sickened more than 80](http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/keyword/ancient-mariner).

With nothing else going for her, the once-proud vessel was acquired at public auction, “purchased by the South Florida Divers Club of Hollywood for $6,000 and donated to Broward County’s artificial reef program. In June of 1991, the _Nemesis_, now called _Ancient Mariner_, was sunk as an artificial reef off Deerfield Beach.”

[![Image 139: An old, white passenger ship with a red diving flag on its smokestack sails on the sea alongside a small pilot boat](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/nemesis-aka-ancient-mariner-2-via-dixie-diver.jpg?resize=519%2C260&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/nemesis-aka-ancient-mariner-2-via-dixie-diver/)

She is a [popular](https://www.force-e.com/go-diving/boat-dive-sites/ancient-mariner/) dive site today [resting just 50-70 feet deep](https://www.southfloridadiving.com/dive-sites/wreck-dive-sites/ancient-mariner/). “A large Goliath Grouper guards the wreckage and can usually be found in the wheelhouse.”

[![Image 140: Ancient Mariner dive map in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, shows location of sunken shipwreck with depth levels marked, accessible via Hillsboro Inlet with high current](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/nemesis-aka-ancient-mariner.jpg?resize=519%2C333&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/nemesis-aka-ancient-mariner/)

Of her sisters, _USCGC Ariadne (WPC-101)_, the last in federal service, was decommissioned 23 Dec. 1968 and sold for scrap the next year. Some went on to overseas service, including _USCGC Galatea, Thetis,_ and _Icarus_, who remained afloat into the late 1980s with the Dominican Republic’s Navy. At least [five of the class](https://books.google.com/books/about/Around_Manhattan_Island_and_Other_Mariti.html?id=4RTxzui1OG4C) were bought by the Circle Line of NYC and converted to local passenger ferry work around the five boroughs. _Daphne_ is thought to be somewhere in Mexican waters as a tug.

Of the 24 various 165s that served in the Coast Guard and Navy across a span of almost a half century, just one, like _Nemesis_ a B-model, remains in some sort of confirmed service.

Commissioned as _USCGC Electra (WPC-187)_ in 1934, she was transferred to the US Navy prior to WWII and renamed _USS Potomac (AG-25)_, serving as FDR’s Presidential Yacht for a decade. Struck from the Navy List in 1946, she was saved in 1980 and is [currently open to the public in Oakland](http://www.usspotomac.org/).

[![Image 141: Potomac boat is docked at pier](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/ex-uss-potomac-ag-25-moored-at-her-berth-the-fdr-pier-at-jack-london-square-oakland-ca-in-2008.jpg?resize=519%2C346&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2015/08/19/warship-wednesday-aug-19-2015-the-first-of-the-bucking-165s/ex-uss-potomac-ag-25-moored-at-her-berth-the-fdr-pier-at-jack-london-square-oakland-ca-in-2008/)

_Ex-USS Potomac (AG-25) moored at her berth, the FDR pier, at Jack London Square, Oakland, CA. in 2008. Still floating in less than 7ft of water, as designed. Photos by Al Riel USS John Rogers.Via Navsource_

As for the Coast Guard, they are increasingly [recycling the old names of the classic 165s](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2017/08/07/uscg-keeps-the-lineage-intact-with-opc-cutter-names/) for their new class of 360-foot Offshore Patrol Cutters so it is possible that _Nemesis_ will pop back up. Further, the service retains a number of old bells from the 165s as artifacts, such as from _USCGC Comanche_, below, which means the bell from _Nemesis_ could very well be ashore somewhere on a Coast Guard base.

[![Image 142: Young female Coast Guardsman stands next to the USS Comanche's bell](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/coast-guard-cutter-comanche-165-1934-with-new-u-s-coast-guard-ceremonial-honor-guard-member.jpg?resize=519%2C346&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/15/warship-wednesday-aug-15-2018-floridas-ancient-sub-buster/coast-guard-cutter-comanche-165-1934-with-new-u-s-coast-guard-ceremonial-honor-guard-member/)

[![Image 144: The corroded metalwork shows the words Vashkarh](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/donskoy-name-plate.jpg?resize=519%2C346&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/donskoy-name-plate/)

_The stern plate of Donskoy, via the Shinil Group, who may be one of the biggest hoaxsters of the 21st century._

It increasingly looks like the shadowy group that intended to salvage the “billions” from the Tsar’s lost semi-armored frigate [_Dmitriy Donskoy_](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/), which made headlines last month, was more flash in the pan than gold in the bank.

[From Gizmodo:](https://gizmodo.com/sunken-warship-said-to-have-billions-in-gold-looks-like-1828264435)

> More bizarre twists and outrageous claims kept coming, culminating in a July 26 press conference in which company President Choi Yong-seok told reporters, “there’s no way for us to figure out whether there would be gold coins or bars on the Donskoi,” and that the company’s previous claims were based on speculation and media reports. He also said he’d only become president a few hours before the conference and the other members of leadership had resigned.

It should be noted that this is not the first time that treasure hunters have promised big bucks from the Tsar’s doomed 2nd Pacific Squadron only to come up short. In 1980, Japanese salvors located the armored cruiser _Admiral Nakhimov_ and [pulled up](http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,951534,00.html) an unspecified amount of gold bullion, platinum ingots, and British gold sovereigns– over the howls of the Soviets. The ship [reportedly](https://www.upi.com/Archives/1980/10/08/Japanese-to-salvage-38-billion-treasure-from-Czarist-wreck/8818339825600/) carried 16 platinum bars, 48 gold bars and about 5,000 pounds of British gold coins. The funny thing is– the ingots shown off in 1980 were later [found to be made out of lead](https://www.gettyimages.com/event/diry-track-517481049#/contemporary-painting-of-king-richard-iii-2013-based-on-the-facial-picture-id476738687).

[Warship Wednesday, Aug. 8, 2018: Giuseppe, how many seaplanes you packing?](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/)

_Here at LSOZI, we are going to [take off every Wednesday for a look at the old steam/diesel navies of the 1859-1946 period](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/category/warship-wednesday/) and will profile a different ship each week. These ships have a life, a tale all their own, which sometimes takes them to the strangest places. – Christopher Eger_

**Warship Wednesday, Aug. 8, 2018: Giuseppe, how many seaplanes you packing?**

[![Image 145: R. N. Giuseppe Miraglia at sea, in black and white](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-6.jpg?resize=519%2C346&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-6/)

_(1500×1000)_

Here we see the Regia Marina’s very proud seaplane carrier, _Giuseppe Miraglia,_ at anchor in the 1930s. A true-life example of what today would be seen as a dieselpunk aesthetic, the Italian navy views her as an important predecessor of their modern pocket carriers– _Cavour_ and _Giuseppe Garibaldi_— today.

Italy got into the seaplane tender biz in February 1915 when they bought the aging 392-ft./7,100-ton Spanish-built freighter _Quarto_ and, as _Europa_, converted the vessel to operate a half-dozen or so FBA flying boats. Taking part in the Battle of the Strait of Otranto against the bottled-up Austro-Hungarian fleet in 1917, she was discarded after the war.

[![Image 146: Aircraft carrier HMS Furious launches the Squadron of Sopwith Camel aircraft in 1918](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-europa-in-service-1915-1920.jpg?resize=800%2C766&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-europa-in-service-1915-1920/)

_Italian seaplane carrier Europa, in service 1915-1920. Note her method of flying boat storage_

Fast forward to the mid-1920s, and Italian rivals Britain and France had newer and more modern seaplane carriers (such as _HMAS/HMS Albatross_ and _Commandant Teste_, the latter carrying 26 aircraft) on the drawing board. This left the Italian Navy with a need for a warship that could pack a lot of (sea)planes once again.

In 1925, Rome bought the incomplete passenger/mail steamer _Citta di Messina_ and, sending her to the _Regio Arsenale Della Spezia_ for completion, produced _Giuseppe Miraglia_.

The vessel was renamed in honor of Tenente di vascello Giuseppe Miraglia, an early Italian naval aviator killed in an accident in 1915 at age 27.

[![Image 147: Man in uniform, captured in a monochrome portrait](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/tenente-di-vascello-giuseppe-miraglia.jpg?resize=419%2C600&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/tenente-di-vascello-giuseppe-miraglia/)

_This guy_

Early in the war, he made headlines in the country by leading his seaplane squadron over Austrian-held Trieste in a raid that was widely celebrated.

She wasn’t a giant ship, just under 400-feet long with a light draft of 4,500-tons. But _Miraglia_ was fast enough for naval use (21 knots) and with enough room for as many as 20 seaplanes of assorted sizes.

For this, she was well-equipped with two below-deck hangars in what was to be the steamship’s holds, each equipped with catapults and cranes for launching and recovery, respectively. Inside the hangars were room for spare parts including fresh engines, a few spare aircraft in “knocked down” crated condition, tools, and handling equipment.

[![Image 148: The Danish coastal defense ship Olfert Fischer is shown in a black-and-white full shot, with a seaplane hanging to the side](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-note-hangar.jpg?resize=519%2C272&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-note-hangar/)

_Note her hangar arrangement fore and aft of her stack_

Many of the planned staterooms which originally were meant for 1st and 2nd class passengers were completed for aircrew instead. A central ordnance magazine and avfuel storage were accessible from each hangar.

[![Image 149: Italian seaplane carrier Giuseppe Miraglia shown in Naples in the 1930s](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-taranto.jpg?resize=519%2C513&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-taranto/)

_All those Macchis…_

The twin hangars could each hold 5-6 Macchi M.18AR seaplanes with their wings folded while additional aircraft “parking” was available topside for a couple extra boats.

[![Image 150: Men in white uniforms stand in front of a biplane with the word R-3 on it](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/machi-18.jpg?resize=519%2C324&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/machi-18/)

A pusher-style biplane flying boat, the M.18AR was one of the more successful “combat” seaplanes of the 1920s and 30s, serving not only with the Italians but with the [Spanish Navy](https://sites.google.com/site/buquesgce/aeonautica-naval/7-macchi-m-18)‘s early seaplane carrier _Dédalo_ (Dedalus) during the Civil War in that country as well as against Moroccan rebels, but also with the [Paraguayan Navy](http://www.aeroflight.co.uk/tag/macchi-m-18ar) during the Chaco War.

The open cockpit three-seat scout bombers were the staple of the _Aviazione per la Regina Marina_ for much of the interwar period, capable of toting a few small bombs and a 7.7mm machine gun aloft with a 300~ mile combat radius.

[![Image 151: Torpedoed Ship, with explosions happening around the scene, accompanied by planes flying in the sky](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/flight-of-macchi-18ars-with-the-aeronc3a1utica-naval-espac3b1ola-spanish.jpg?resize=519%2C313&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/flight-of-macchi-18ars-with-the-aeronautica-naval-espanola-spanish/)

_A flight of Macchi 18ARs with the Aeronáutica Naval Española, impressive airpower for the roaring 20s._

By 1930, the Macchi aircraft were replaced largely with Cantoni 25 AR seaplanes and, after 1937, with the smaller but more modern IMAM Ro.43, which at least had a closed cockpit and two machine guns rather than just one– although carried no bombs.

[![Image 152: Black and white photograph of an IMAM Ro.43 floatplane being hoisted onto the Giuseppe Miraglia](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/imam-ro-43-seaplane.jpg?resize=519%2C367&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/imam-ro-43-seaplane/)

_Recovering an IMAM Ro.43 seaplane, the standard Italian Navy’s floatplane that flew from not only Miraglia but also all her cruisers and battleships from 1937 onward_

_Miraglia’s_ topside deck was protected by 50mm of armor to stave off air attacks not scared off by her AAA suite of a dozen Breda machine guns while a quartet of 4-inch guns could take shots at closing destroyers or torpedo boats. She had a side belt of between 70 and 80mm (sources vary).

_Miraglia_ entered service 1 November 1927 and was used in the disgrace that was the Italo-Ethiopian War in the late 1930s to transport aircraft to the theatre.

[![Image 153: HMS Argus, with planes, navigates the ocean in a black and white photograph](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia.jpg?resize=519%2C271&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia/)

_With six Macchi seaplanes on deck, underway_

[![Image 154: Aircraft carrier in black and white, navigating the waters and expelling black smoke](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-4.jpg?resize=519%2C389&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-4/)

_Note the Macchi ready to cat. The ship carried one Gagnotto-made catapult forward…_

[![Image 155: USS Langley ACV-1 in the 1920s, featuring two planes on the deck and other boats and docks in the background](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-2.jpg?resize=519%2C371&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-2/)

_…And another aft. Also, note the 4-inch gun under the cat on the aft stdb quarter_

[![Image 156: R. N. G. Miraglia, a monochromatic exterior shot of a warship on the water, the ship has a tall mast and is light-colored with visible portholes](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-3.jpg?resize=519%2C415&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-3/)

[![Image 157: A battle ship in a harbor with people lined up on the deck in the past](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/nh-111421-italian-ship-giuseppe-miraglia-italy-cvan-circa-1935.jpeg?resize=519%2C386&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/nh-111421-italian-ship-giuseppe-miraglia-italy-cvan-circa-1935/)

_Italian ship GIUSEPPE MIRAGLIA. Italy – CVAN. Circa 1935. Note the seaplanes on her hangar decks. NH 111421_

When WWII came, she somehow managed to not catch a British torpedo or American bomb while serving in the Mediterranean although she was present in the harbor for the raid on Taranto in 1940. She spent most of the war as a transport and testbed, rather than in operations.

Later in the conflict, the zippy little Reggiane Re.2000 Falco I “Catapultabile” monoplane, which could be catapulted off by not recovered by the vessel, made an appearance on the ship.

[![Image 158: Fighter plane sits on a ship as crew lines the deck, with ocean in the background](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/a-reggiane-re-2000-on-the-italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia.jpg?resize=519%2C363&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/a-reggiane-re-2000-on-the-italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia/)

_The Re.2000 Catapultabile (MM.8281) on a topside catapult of Giuseppe Miraglia ready for take-off, May 1942. Less than a dozen of these variants were used during WWII. The planes were planned for the unfinished 27,000-ton Italian aircraft carrier L’ Aquila but cut their teeth on Miraglia._

[![Image 159: An airplane and crew are on the deck of a warship](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/a-reggiane-re-2000-on-the-italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia1.jpg?resize=519%2C345&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/a-reggiane-re-2000-on-the-italian-seaplane-carrier-giuseppe-miraglia-2/)[![Image 160: Aircraft is on a catapult of the Raimondo Montecuccoli-class cruiser](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/the-re-2000-catapultabile-mm-8281-on-the-catapult-of-giuseppe-miraglia-ready-for-take-off-may-1942.jpg?resize=519%2C389&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/the-re-2000-catapultabile-mm-8281-on-the-catapult-of-giuseppe-miraglia-ready-for-take-off-may-1942/)

Following the shit-canning of Mussolini, _Miraglia_ sailed to Malta in 1943 to be interned under British guns and served the rest of the war as a receiving ship for Italian sailors from smaller vessels.

Meanwhile, Italy’s first planned aircraft carrier– a respectable 772-foot leviathan by the name of _L’Aquila_ (Eagle) converted from an unfinished ocean liner– was left under construction at Genoa.

[![Image 161: Aircraft carrier under construction in a dry dock](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/italian-aircraft-carrier-aquila-in-drydock-at-genoa-in-1942.jpg?resize=800%2C546&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2021/08/02/italy-finally-has-an-aircraft-carrier/italian-aircraft-carrier-aquila-in-drydock-at-genoa-in-1942/)

Italian aircraft carrier Aquila in drydock at Genoa in 1942. She would never be completed

Although it was envisioned she would carry up to 56 aircraft, the Italian eagle was never completed and finally scrapped at La Spezia in 1952. A sistership, _Sparviero_, never even got that far, making _Miraglia_ the sole Italian aviation ship fielded in WWII.

[![Image 162: Aircraft carrier Trieste after its scuttling in 1945](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/the-unfinished-italian-aircraft-carrier-aquila-tied-up-at-la-spezia-sometime-following-italys-surrender-in-wwii.jpg?resize=519%2C322&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/the-unfinished-italian-aircraft-carrier-aquila-tied-up-at-la-spezia-sometime-following-italys-surrender-in-wwii/)

_The unfinished Italian aircraft carrier “Aquila” tied up at La Spezia sometime following Italy’s surrender in WWII._

[![Image 163: War-damaged aircraft carrier in bay, circa 1945 in monochrome](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-aircraft-carrier-aquila-in-1950.jpg?resize=696%2C460&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-aircraft-carrier-aquila-in-1950/)

_Italian aircraft carrier Aquila in 1950, pending her conversion to razor blades_

Following the end of the war, with the general disfavor of seaplanes and seaplane carriers of the time, _Miraglia_ was retained at Taranto as a PT boat tender until 1950 when she was disposed of. _Jane’s_, in their often confusing 1946-47 volume, noted that she was to be refitted as a supply ship.

[![Image 164: Giuseppe Miraglia 1946-47 Janes listing](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/20190519_170211-e1558327259871.jpg?resize=519%2C389&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/20190519_170211/)

_Giuseppe Miraglia, 1946-47 Janes listing, where she was one of the few Italian ships left from WWII_

**The spark rekindled**

Italian Naval Aviation languished for a full decade following VE-Day, only restarting on a limited scale when a few Bell-Augusta AB-47G helicopters were handed over to the Navy for shipboard service in 1956.

By 1969, _Vittorio Veneto_, a so-called “helicopter cruiser,” was in service, capable of carrying six SH-3D Sea Kings or larger numbers of smaller whirlybirds.

[![Image 165: Two naval ships navigate a narrow waterway near buildings and walls, with a coastal scene in the distance](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/vittorio-veneto-taranto.jpg?resize=519%2C357&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/vittorio-veneto-taranto/)

_Vittorio Veneto was all cruiser in the front…_

[![Image 166: Italian Navy destroyer Vittorio Veneto (550) in the open sea](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/1704x1176-its-c550-vittorio-veneto-view-from-behind-with-raised-deck-and-hangar-beneath-e1533675141920.jpg?resize=519%2C358&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/1704x1176-its-c550-vittorio-veneto-view-from-behind-with-raised-deck-and-hangar-beneath/)

_But a party in the back…ITS Vittorio Veneto (C550) view from the stern with raised deck and hangar beneath._

Finally, in 1990 the Italian government placed an order for several AV-8B Harriers for use on the newly completed light aircraft carrier _Garibaldi_, returning the country’s fleet to a fixed-wing capability that it hadn’t seen since _Miraglia_ steamed for exile in Malta in 1943.

Today, it is thought that the carrier _Cavour_ will carry a squadron of [operational Italian F-35Bs](https://theaviationist.com/2018/01/18/here-is-italys-first-f-35b-lightning-ii-flying-in-full-italian-navy-markings-for-the-first-time-today/) by 2023, almost a century after _Miraglia_ was conceived.

[![Image 167: Aircraft carrier Cavour of the Italian Navy on the ocean](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/italian-aircraft-carrier-cavour.jpg?resize=519%2C345&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/italian-aircraft-carrier-cavour/)

_Italian aircraft carrier Cavour_

**Specs**:

[![Image 168: The Giuseppe Miraglia is an Italian seaplane carrier depicted in a blueprint rendering](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/giuseppe-miraglia.jpg?resize=519%2C398&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/08/08/warship-wednesday-aug-8-2018-giuseppe-how-many-seaplanes-you-packing/giuseppe-miraglia/)

 Displacement, full load: 5.913 t

 Length: 397.72 ft.

 Beam: 49.18 ft.

 Draft: 19 ft.

 Propulsion: 8 Yarrow water tube boilers, 2 groups of steam turbines with Parsons type reducer, 2 propellers with three blades, 16,700 HP, 430 tons oil.

 Speed: 21 knots

 Crew: (196) not counting airwing, as follows:

 16 officers

 40 NCOs

 140 enlisted

 Armament:

 4 x 102/35 Schneider-Armstrong naval rifles

 12 x 13.2 mm Breda machine guns

 Airwing:

 2 Gagnotto steam catapults in bow and stern

 2 aircraft hangars for 5-6 planes with folded wings (total of 11 seaplanes)

 2 depots for 3 dismantled aircraft, each

 17 Macchi M.18AR seaplanes (1927-30), 20 Cantoni 25 AR seaplanes (1931-36) up to 20 IMAM Ro.43s (1937-43)

[Warship Wednesday, July 25, 2018: Tsar Nicky’s lost (crypto) millions?](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/)

_Here at LSOZI, we are going to take off every [Wednesday for a look at the old steam/diesel navies of the 1859-1946 period and will profile a different ship each week](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/category/warship-wednesday/). These ships have a life, a tale all their own, which sometimes takes them to the strangest places. – Christopher Eger_

**Warship Wednesday, July 25, 2018: Tsar Nicky’s lost (crypto) millions?**

[![Image 169: Battleship of black color is in the sea](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/donskoy-colorised-by-diego-mar-postales-navales.jpg?resize=519%2C349&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/donskoy-colorised-by-diego-mar-postales-navales/)

_Colorized by my good friend Diego Mar of Postales Navales_

Here we see the semi-armored frigate (often classified as a cruiser) _Dmitriy Donskoy_ (or, _Dmitri Donskoi_) of the Tsarist Imperial Navy in her classic black and buff scheme. Note the Romanov double eagle crest in yellow– house colors– on her bow.

She was the last warship claimed by the military fiasco that was the Battle of Tsushima in 1905 and notably has popped back in the news last week with her (re)discovery by a Singapore-based South Korean treasure-hunting group, thus:

[![Image 170: The corroded metalwork shows the words Vashkarh](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/donskoy-name-plate.jpg?resize=519%2C346&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/donskoy-name-plate/)

_Via the Shinil Group_

But we are getting ahead of ourselves. Let’s get some context.

In the late 1870s, the Russian navy was fairly powerful, the proud owner of several U.S.-built coastal monitors ready to mix it up with anything sent into their waters, and a reasonable fleet of blue water steam vessels. What they really needed, however, were armored blue water ships capable of ranging far and wide. Enter the armored frigate _Minin_, some 295-feet overall and 6,100-tons, she was capable of 14-knots and carried a quartet of 8-inch guns and as much as 7-inches of locally made iron armor. Not bad for 1878. At the same time came the Russian cruiser _General Admiral_, considered the world’s first armored cruiser, combining an armor belt with an armored protective deck in a 285-foot/5,038-ton package capable of making 12 knots.

[![Image 171: Ship with three masts and two smokestacks sailing on the water](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/russian-cruiser-general-admiral-is-considered-the-worlds-first-armored-cruiser-combining-an-armor-belt-with-an-armored-protective-deck-loc.jpg?resize=519%2C384&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/russian-cruiser-general-admiral-is-considered-the-worlds-first-armored-cruiser-combining-an-armor-belt-with-an-armored-protective-deck-loc/)

_General Admiral, shown in New York in 1893– but we’ll get to that (LOC photo)_

By 1880, the Admiralty ordered the follow-on _Dmitriy Donskoy_, named after St. Dmitry of the Don who beat the Tartars at the Battle of Kulikovo in the 14th century, one of the largest battles of the Middle Ages and the event that signaled the beginning of the end of the Mongol Yoke over Rus.

[![Image 172: Russian warriors marching through a field of tall grass](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitriy-donskoy-st-dmitry-of-the-don-who-beat-the-tartars-at-the-battle-of-kulikovo.jpg?resize=519%2C274&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitriy-donskoy-st-dmitry-of-the-don-who-beat-the-tartars-at-the-battle-of-kulikovo/)

_The guy on the white horse…_

She was the fifth Russian naval ship since 1771 to carry the name– and the last until 2000.

Beefier than _General Admiral_ and about even 10 feet longer and 100-tons heavier (she used heavier steel armor ordered abroad from Cammell Laird to include a belt and armored deck) than _Minin_, the new armored frigate had more economical engines coupled with larger coal bunkers that gave her three times the range of _Minin_ and a speed of 16-knots (making 16.16 on trials). She could travel for a week at full speed and up to 30 days at a more pedestrian 10-knots. Then, in 1883, came her half-sister, the more refined _Vladimir Monomakh_, a tweaked 306-foot/6,000-ton vessel to the same layout.

All four of these experimental ships had copper sheathed hulls to cut down on drydocking– and allowing more distant deployments– and were heavily ship-rigged on three wooden masts for extending their range under sail. Their props were originally designed to be lifted to prevent drag while under canvas, but that did not work in practice.

[![Image 173: An old black and white photograph shows a ship in the water near land](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitriydonskoy4.jpg?resize=519%2C346&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitriydonskoy4/)Referred to as armored cruisers by the rest of the world, there was a legit concern (mainly by the British) at the time that these ships would create havoc on sea lanes as commerce raiders in the event of war.

_Donskoy_ spent the first two years of her career with the Mediterranean Sea squadron, then in 1887 transferred to the Pacific, where Russia was eagerly looking to expand.

An 1889 modification saw her wooden masts replaced by lighter steel ones, followed by another tour of the Med, and by 1891 she was back in the Pacific and would sail the world extensively for several years.

[![Image 174: HMS Rover, a composite screw corvette of the Royal Navy, photographed on the water in the late 19th century](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitriydonskoy5.jpg?resize=519%2C447&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitriydonskoy5/)

She participated in the World’s Columbian Exposition in 1893 as the flagship of the Russian squadron, sailing up the Hudson along with the already-mentioned _General Admiral_, gunboat _Rynda_ (c1885/3,537t) and the new and mighty armored cruiser [_Admiral Nakhimov_](https://wp.me/p1ttYu-2Pt) (c1888/8,609t), the latter a Warship Wednesday alum.

[![Image 175: A large steam powered warship is sitting on calm water](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitri-donskoi-russian-navy_lc-d4-21190.jpg?resize=519%2C374&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitri-donskoi-russian-navy_lc-d4-21190/)

_Dmitri Donskoi, Russian navy\_LOC-D4-21190_

[![Image 176: The black and white photograph depicts the Russian battleship Petr Veliky, a warship of the Imperial Russian Navy, with its tall masts and complex rigging dominating the scene](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitri-donskoi-russian-navy_lc-d4-21191.jpg?resize=519%2C421&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitri-donskoi-russian-navy_lc-d4-21191/)

_Dmitri Donskoi, Russian navy\_LOC-D4-21191_

Her officers were a hit with the New York social crowd.

[![Image 177: Captain of the Russian Navy wearing navy-blue uniform, medals, and white cap stands with hands together and sword to his left](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/captain-of-cruiser-dimitry-donskoy-russia-full-dress-navy-dmitry-donskoy.jpg?resize=519%2C407&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/captain-of-cruiser-dimitry-donskoy-russia-full-dress-navy-dmitry-donskoy/)

_Capt. 1st Rank NA Zelenoy, skipper of the Donskoy, in his full uniform, colorized photo from Detriot Post Card company, via LOC_

In 1895 she was extensively modified with new engines and boilers, and her armament updated, shipping for the Far East again the next year, carrying a white scheme for a time.

[![Image 178: The crowd celebrates the launching of the British ship in the water](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/ironclad-irn-dmitrii-donskoi-picture-at-the-opening-of-the-vladivostok-drydockoctober-7th-1897.jpg?resize=519%2C376&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/ironclad-irn-dmitrii-donskoi-picture-at-the-opening-of-the-vladivostok-drydockoctober-7th-1897/)

_Ironclad IRN Dmitrii Donskoi picture at the opening of the Vladivostok Drydock, October 7th, 1897_

[![Image 179: White-painted ship has rigging of pennants and is afloat](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitriydonskoy.jpg?resize=519%2C348&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitriydonskoy/)

She would spend six years in Vladivostok, then the new Russian enclave at Port Arthur (which they basically stole from the Japanese), and her crew formed a naval battalion that participated in the Boxer rebellion.

[![Image 180: A battle scene shows Russian soldiers fighting, with some firing a cannon, depicted in a sketch](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/russian-sailors-defending-a-barricade-before-the-peking-legation-1900-in-boxer-rebellion-via-the-london-illustrated-news.jpeg?resize=519%2C314&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/russian-sailors-defending-a-barricade-before-the-peking-legation-1900-in-boxer-rebellion-via-the-london-illustrated-news/)

_Russian Sailors Defending A Barricade Before The Peking Legation 1900 in Boxer Rebellion via the London Illustrated News_

At the end of 1901, she returned to the Baltic again for another refit and armament swap (honestly, she changed her batteries so much that it is irrelevant to cover each update, check the specs at the bottom for more details).

She was aging, slow for her times, and poorly armed for her size, and a 1900 Jane’s entry characterized her as such.

[![Image 181: Dmitri Donskoi (1883), old Russian armored cruiser with listed specifications: 5,880 tons displacement, 550 complement, 295 ft length, 52 ft beam, 25 ft max draught](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/donskoy-janes.jpg?resize=426%2C484&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/donskoy-janes/)Early 1904 saw her leaving for the Far East once again with the cruiser _Almaz_ and a group of new destroyers, but they only got as far as the Red Sea before war came with Japan– over Port Arthur– and she was recalled to the Baltic.

With the war going exceptionally bad for the Russians militarily, and the Tsar’s Pacific Squadron largely bottled up behind minefields and Japanese blockade at Port Arthur, the Baltic Fleet suddenly became dubbed the 2nd Pacific Squadron and soon received orders to sail to the Far East and throw down. The epic story is told best by Constantine Pleshakov in his “The Tsar’s Last Armada: The Epic Voyage to the Battle of Tsushima.”

[![Image 182: The Tsar's Last Armada book cover is displayed on a table](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/20180724_203721.jpg?resize=519%2C692&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/20180724_203721/)

_It’s a good read…_

In the book, _Donskoy_ appears a dozen or more times, derided by Vice Adm. Rozhestvensky as the “cabbie” of the fleet due to her slow speed. First, she caught a broadside from her own fleet in the Baltic (!) during a confusing nighttime skirmish that injured several men and, as British trawlers were harmed, forced the ill-fated warships to sail all the way around the Cape of Good Hope rather than via the London-controlled Suez Canal.

Then, _Donskoy_ became the great fisherman of the fleet in Madagascar– catching some 1,800 pounds of fish in one go via nets but losing a man to a shark. Then came her officers’ rather racy involvement with the nurses of the hospital ship _Orel_. Anyway, pick up the book, it’s a great read.

![Image 183: The Russo-Japanese war's route map shows the movements of the Russian fleet in the Pacific Ocean and around the globe in red, brown, and blue](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/battle_of_japan_sea_route_of_baltic_fleet_nt.png?resize=700%2C500)

_The blue line…_

Now, in the third act, we have our valiant frigate’s destruction in the Strait of Korea. Part of a four-ship column of cruisers under the flag of the unpopular but politically connected Rear-Admiral Oskar Enkvist– she joined _Oleg_, _Aurora_, and her sister _Monomakh_ and were tasked with guarding the auxiliaries in the rear column of the fleet by Rozhdestvensky.

Escaping the carnage of the main fleet action, he ordered the group to make their way as best they could to Vladivostok. The Admiral later caught up to them in the leaking torpedo boat _Buiny_ but during the night of May 27/28, they became separated again. Meanwhile, the Japanese were busy hunting the stragglers. _Monomakh_ was torpedoed by a Japanese torpedo boat in the night and surrendered the next day. The _Zhemchug_, _Aurora_, and _Oleg_ damaged managed to make it to Manila to be interned by the Americans under the guns of the old monitor _[USS Monadnock (BM-3)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2014/04/30/warship-wednesday-april-30-of-great-repairs-and-shallow-waters-the-uss-monadnock/)._

By the morning of the 28th, _Donskoy_, now just accompanied by two torpedo boats– _Bedovy_ and _Grozny_— found the wounded Rozhdestvensky on his languishing _Buiny_ and transferred him, along with the _Donskoy_‘s surgeon, to the _Bedovy_ for the final 400-mile run to safety in Vladivostok. _Donskoy_ remained behind to cover the admiral’s retreat and rescue the crew from _Buiny_ then sink her with gunfire. Overall, the ship had more than 300 survivors aboard, mostly from the lost battleship _Oslyabya_.

Ultimately, Rozhestvensky was captured after his new torpedo boat suffered an engineering casualty later that morning, but _Donskoy_ pressed on alone, filled with survivors she picked up along the way. By 5 p.m. she was sighted by the pursuing Japanese and, some two hours later, was some 30 nautical miles south of Ulleungdo (Dajelet) Island. Over the next two hours, she dueled with the Japanese cruisers _Otowa_ (3,000t) and _Niitaka_ (3,400 tons), together with the destroyers _Asagiri_, _Shirakumo,_ and _Fubuki_. It was a hell of a fight by all accounts and the Japanese caught a few rounds in return fire– a rarety in the typical Russo-Japanese exchange.

[![Image 184: A battle ship that is on fire, and has water spraying from the ship because it has been struck](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitriydonskoy-sink.jpg?resize=519%2C356&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitriydonskoy-sink/)

[![Image 185: A warship is embroiled in a sea battle, with explosions and smoke obscuring parts of the ship and the surrounding water](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/zaikin-a-yu-born-1954-the-last-fight-of-dmitry-donskoy-1995.jpg?resize=519%2C412&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/zaikin-a-yu-born-1954-the-last-fight-of-dmitry-donskoy-1995/)

_Zaikin A.Yu. (born 1954) “The last fight of Dmitry Donskoy,” 1995_

This left the old _Donskoy_ battered and her skipper, the valiant Capt.1st Rank Ivan Nikolayevich Lebedev, a veteran with some 38 years of service behind him, on his literal last leg, one of some 190 casualties suffered in the final act of Tsushima.

From a Russian memoir of the hellish scene on _Donskoy_, of her XO, Capt. 2nd rank Konstantin Platonovich Blokhin, being called to the bridge:

> The senior officer was on deck when one of the sailors flew up to him and, choking on words, reported:
> 
> 
> “Your Honor … the commander asks you.”
> 
> 
> Blokhin immediately climbed to the bridge and, peering into the warped and dilapidated cabin, for a moment was dumbfounded. The whole deck shone with fresh blood. Lieutenant Durnovo, leaning against the wall, sat motionless, bent, as if thinking about something, but he and his cap had a skull and horribly pinked frozen brain. The helmsman Quartermaster Polyakov curled up at the binnacle. Lieutenant Giers was lying with his belly open. Above these corpses, gritting his teeth in pain, Lieutenant commander towered alone, barely holding onto the handles of the wheel. He had a through wound in his thigh with a bone fracture.
> 
> 
> In addition, his entire body was wounded with small fragments. He stood on one leg and tried to hold the cruiser on the course, himself unaware that the steering gear was broken and that the ship was steadily rolling to the right. Seeing the senior officer, he raised his eyebrows in surprise and said with blue lips:
> 
> 
> “I hand over the command…”
> 
> 
> “I’ll arrange for you to be transferred, Ivan Nikolayevich, to the dressing station.”
> 
> 
> “Do not. I’ll stay here. Try to get to the shade of the island. Do not hand over the ship. Better to scuttle her.”

And with that, Lebedev died and his battered ship limped closer to Ulleungdo Island and was scuttled by her crew in deep water some two miles offshore on the morning of the 29th, sending her survivors ashore where the Japanese took them, prisoner.

Blokhin survived, later becoming a rear admiral. Her mine officer, Lt. Alexander Oskarovich Stark (whose father, Vice Adm. Oskar Viktorovich Stark had ironically been in command of the _1st_ Pacific Squadron at Port Arthur), went on to command the cruiser _Bayan_ in the Baltic during WWI and died in exile (along with his dad) in Finland in the 1920s.

As for Rozhestvensky, after ducking a death sentence at a court-martial after the war, he lived out the last years of his life in St Petersburg as a recluse and died in 1909 of a bad heart, aged 60. He had lost 4,380 men and 21 vessels– including an amazing seven battleships– over the course of about 24-hours, while another seven of his warships were captured by the Japanese along with a staggering 5,900 men– to include the survivors of _Donskoy_, of course. The Japanese lost no major ships and suffered about 700 mixed casualties in what could be called the all-time benchmark for a decisive naval victory.

Fast forward a few years, and the stories of the gold started to come out, with the legend going that the vessels were piled high with a mini-fortune to be used to buy coal and supplies aboard as needed because Russia had precisely zero coaling stations between the Baltic and Vladivostok.

In 1933, an author named Garry Berg published a hard-to-find pamphlet, “600 Billion in Water,” holding that four ships of the Rozhestvensky’s 2nd Pacific Squadron sunk at the Battle of Tsushima had a horde of gold, then worth US $5 million, with the largest portions on two cruisers– $2 million carried on _Admiral Nakhimov_, and another $2 million on _Donskoy_. In 1980, Japanese salvors located _Nakhimov_ and [pulled up](http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,951534,00.html) an unspecified amount of gold bullion, platinum ingots, and British gold sovereigns– over the howls of the Soviets. The ship [reportedly](https://www.upi.com/Archives/1980/10/08/Japanese-to-salvage-38-billion-treasure-from-Czarist-wreck/8818339825600/) carried 16 platinum bars, 48 gold bars, and about 5,000 pounds of British gold coins. The funny thing is– the ingots shown off in 1980 were later [found to be made out of lead](https://www.gettyimages.com/event/diry-track-517481049#/contemporary-painting-of-king-richard-iii-2013-based-on-the-facial-picture-id476738687).

In 2001, a South Korean group said they found _Donskoy_, which is rumored to hold 5,500 boxes of gold bullion and 200 tons of gold coins aboard her– an incredible cache that today is worth some $130 billion if it is to be believed. The ROK-government-run Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology followed up with a claim on the wreck a few years later.

However, no one has been able to salve it.

Now, the Singapore-based Shinil Group has once again stirred the _Donskoy_ pot, [saying they have located her stern](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/shinil-group-found-the-russian-first-class-armored-cruiser-donskoii-which-sank-near-koreas-ulleungdo-for-113-years-300682018.html) (she is nearly broken in two) at N37°-29′.2″ E130°-56′.3″ to be precise.

“The bottom of _Donskoy_ is about 40 degrees on the slope of the seabed with its stern 380 meters below the water level, and its bow is at 430 meters. One-third of the stern is bombarded, and the hull is severely damaged. It is a half-broken situation. However, the upper deck of the wooden hull is almost untouched. The armor on the side of the hull is also well preserved, while the anchors, guns, and machine guns remain in place. In addition, all three of the masts and the two chimneys are broken, there was also a partial attacked trail of marking on the sides.”

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QEFId25LMk0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QEFId25LMk0)

Now, as reported by the [Singapore Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/treasure-ship-claim-by-firm-which-lists-singapore-address-on-website-raises-eyebrows), the group is offering a swing at the “Donskoi International” crypto currency exchange providing tokens called Shinil Gold Coins (SGCs), backed apparently by gold futures on the wreck, which makes the whole idea of the 2nd Pacific Squadron’s ridiculous 18,000-mile journey to Valhalla seem like an innovative idea in comparison…

As for the Russians, after spending some 95 years trying to forget _Donskoy_, they renamed the 20-year-old _TK-208_, a huge Project 941 Akula (NATO: Typhoon-class) ballistic missile submarine built in 1980, as _Dmitriy Donskoy_.

[![Image 186: A large black submarine is sailing on the sea under the blue sky](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/tk-208-a-huge-project-941-nato-typhoon-class-ballistic-missile-subarine-built-in-1980-as-dmitriy-donskoy-after-2000.jpg?resize=519%2C281&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/tk-208-a-huge-project-941-nato-typhoon-class-ballistic-missile-subarine-built-in-1980-as-dmitriy-donskoy-after-2000/)

She is the largest submarine in the world in regular fleet service, assigned to the Northern Fleet at Severodvinsk, and the last of her class on active duty. Her aging R-39 ballistic missiles were replaced with launchers for the new RSM-56 Bulava SLBM and she has been testing them out over the past several years.

**Specs:**

[![Image 187: The side view diagram of a sailing ship shows the rigging, masts, and smokestacks](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/dmitriydonskoy-class-vladimir-monomakh.jpg?resize=519%2C325&ssl=1)](http://laststandonzombieisland.com/2018/07/25/warship-wednesday-july-25-2018-tsar-nickys-lost-crypto-millions/dmitriydonskoy-class-vladimir-monomakh/)Displacement 5800 t, 6200 fl

_(1886)_

If you liked this column, please consider joining the International Naval Research Organization (INRO), Publishers of Warship International

They are possibly one of the best sources of naval study, images, and fellowship you can find. [http://www.warship.org/membership.htm](http://www.warship.org/membership.htm)

The International Naval Research Organization is a non-profit corporation dedicated to the encouragement of the study of naval vessels and their histories, principally in the era of iron and steel warships (about 1860 to date). Its purpose is to provide information and a means of contact for those interested in warships.

With more than 50 years of scholarship, Warship International, the written tome of the INRO has published hundreds of articles, most of which are unique in their sweep and subject.

PRINT still has its place. If you LOVE warships you should belong.

I’m a member, so should you be!

3.title: USCGC Dione - Wikiwand
3.description: USCGC Dione (WPC-107) was a Thetis-class patrol boat operated by the United States Coast Guard from 1934 to 1963; she was designated a cutter. Her and the other...
3.content:
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USCGC_Dione&action=edit&section=0&oldformat=true)
**USCGC _Dione_ (WPC-107)** was a [_Thetis_-class patrol boat](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Thetis-class_patrol_boat "Thetis-class patrol boat") operated by the [United States Coast Guard](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Coast_Guard "United States Coast Guard") from 1934 to 1963; she was designated a [cutter](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Coast_Guard_Cutter "United States Coast Guard Cutter"). Her and the other members of the _Thetis_ class were designed to enforce [Prohibition in the United States](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States") by stopping [rum-runners](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rum-running "Rum-running"); her class had been designed to improve on the experiences of previous cutters. Built by the [Manitowoc Shipbuilding Corporation](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Manitowoc_Shipbuilding_Company "Manitowoc Shipbuilding Company") in [Manitowoc, Wisconsin](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Manitowoc,_Wisconsin "Manitowoc, Wisconsin"), _Dione_ was [laid down](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Keel_laying "Keel laying") in November 1933, [launched](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") in June 1934, and [commissioned](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ship_commissioning#Commissioning "Ship commissioning") in October. Prohibition had been repealed in December 1933, so the cutter instead conducted [search and rescue](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Search_and_rescue "Search and rescue") operations out of her station in [Norfolk, Virginia](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Norfolk,_Virginia "Norfolk, Virginia").

**Quick facts** History, United States ...

At the outbreak of the [Second Happy Time](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Second_Happy_Time "Second Happy Time") in January 1942, _Dione_ became the only large ship in the [Fifth Naval District](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_naval_district#Fifth_Naval_District "United States naval district") capable of opposing German [U-boats](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/U-boat "U-boat"). The cutter patrolled the waters off [North Carolina](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/North_Carolina "North Carolina"), which were nicknamed "[Torpedo Alley](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Torpedo_Alley "Torpedo Alley")" due to the high capacity of U-boats operating there. From January to June 1942, she rescued the survivors of torpedoed ships, escorted [Allied convoys](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/List_of_Allied_convoys_during_World_War_II_by_region#North_American_coastal_and_Caribbean_convoys "List of Allied convoys during World War II by region") passing through Torpedo Alley, and hunted sonar pings suspected to have come from U-boats with the goal of sinking one—though the cutter never sank one. In 1945, she was transferred to [New England](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/New_England "New England") with two of her sister ships to help escort surrendered U-boats to American ports, which she did in May when she escorted [_U-1228_](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/German_submarine_U-1228 "German submarine U-1228") to [Portsmouth, New Hampshire](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Portsmouth,_New_Hampshire "Portsmouth, New Hampshire").

_Dione_ served out of Norfolk until she was [decommissioned](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ship_commissioning#Decommissioning "Ship commissioning") in July 1947 due to a lack of personnel. She was recommissioned in February 1951 and became the first Coast Guard Cutter to be stationed in [Freeport, Texas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Freeport,_Texas "Freeport, Texas"). She operated in the [Gulf of Mexico](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"), serving in a search and rescue capacity until she was once more decommissioned in February 1963. The cutter was [placed in reserves](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Reserve_fleet "Reserve fleet") for about a year before being sold as a supply ship in March 1964.

She was operated as [a merchant ship](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#Commercial_service) in the [Gulf Coast region](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Gulf_Coast_of_the_United_States "Gulf Coast of the United States") by three companies and under four different names. She was first known as _**Dione**_ and was operated by the Palmer Decker Boat Company until it was dissolved in September 1967; _Dione_ was seized by a [US Marshal](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Marshals_Service "United States Marshals Service") and auctioned off in December. She was known as _**Big Trouble**_ and owned by Big Trouble Inc. until the company changed its name to Delta Boats Inc. in February 1968, and the ship's name was changed to _**Delta I**._ She was sold to Sabik Inc. in March. _Delta I_ caught fire the next month while underway in the [Caribbean Sea](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea"), and only her [hull](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Hull_(watercraft) "Hull (watercraft)") was salvageable from the fire. The ship was rebuilt, temporarily seized by a US Marshal, and was underway again by March 1970; her name had been changed to _**Al Rashid**_ by that time. She operated under Sabik until 1992, when the former _Dione_ was last seen in service as _Al Rashid_.

[USCGC _Jackson_](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Jackson "USCGC Jackson") in 1927. She was a member of the 125-foot (38 m)_Active_-class patrol boats that preceded the _Thetis_ class.

On 17 January 1920, the [Volstead Act](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Volstead_Act "Volstead Act") went into force in the United States. The law executed the [Eighteenth Amendment](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Eighteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Eighteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), which had been ratified on 16 January 1919. The amendment banned the "manufacture, sale, or transportation" of most alcohol and began the period of [Prohibition in the United States](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States").[[3]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5):11 The Volstead Act was enforced by local [police departments](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Police "Police"), the [Bureau of Prohibition](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bureau_of_Prohibition "Bureau of Prohibition"), the [US Customs Service](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Customs_Service "United States Customs Service"), the [Department of the Treasury](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury "United States Department of the Treasury"), and the Coast Guard.[[4]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5):11 The Coast Guard's role was to prevent [seaborne alcohol smuggling](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rum-running#The_ships "Rum-running"), a job that was initially deemed small and manageable. However, by 1924, the Coast Guard was overwhelmed by the volume of smugglers and struggled to intercept more than five percent of the flow of alcohol.[[4]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5):161-164

Alongside its normal duties, the Coast Guard shifted to impose a [blockade](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Blockade "Blockade") along 5,000 miles (8,000 km) of American coastline. For the role, new patrol boats and [destroyers](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Destroyer "Destroyer")—which had formerly been operated by the [United States Navy](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Navy "United States Navy")—joined the fleet to patrol at sea; Prohibition enforcement had become the first priority for the Coast Guard.[[4]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:29-5):161-164 While the vessels helped fill gaps off the coast, they were expensive to operate and performed poorly. In the 1920s, the Coast Guard began to build purpose-built patrol boats to take over the role of Prohibition enforcement.[[5]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:23-6):382–383 These new cutters varied in size and capability but were used to create a continuous buffer of Prohibition enforcement that stretched from the open ocean to inner harbors.[[6]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:4-7):89,95,99,105

A common tactic by smugglers was to use large, seagoing, [mother ships](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mother_ship "Mother ship") that loitered off the coast and supplied alcohol to smaller boats; the smaller boats then brought the drinks ashore.[[6]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:4-7):108 The Coast Guard ordered the construction of the 125 ft (38 m)-long [_Active_ class](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Active-class_patrol_boat "Active-class patrol boat") cutters in the 1920s to trail and intercept mother ships, and the experience was used to develop the next class of sea-going cutters.[[7]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8):166 The 165-foot (50 m) "B"-class,[[2]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2)[[7]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8):166[[b]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-blcassref-9) named for the cutters' [overall length](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Overall_length "Overall length")[[2]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) and primarily known as the [_Thetis_ class](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Thetis-class_patrol_boat "Thetis-class patrol boat"), was ordered in the 1930s and designed based on results of the _Active_ class' experiences.[[7]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8):166 The design was intended to balance speed, [seaworthiness](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Seakeeping "Seakeeping"), range, radio equipment, and armament.[[8]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-10):100 Eighteen _Thetis_-class cutters were built, and they were large and fast enough to intercept the mother ships.[[6]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:4-7):108 A newspaper article in the _[Oshkosh Northwestern](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Oshkosh\_Northwestern "Oshkosh Northwestern")_ praised the class the day before the launching of _Dione_ and two of her sisters, describing the cutters as having "the latest developments in [marine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Marine_engineering "Marine engineering") and [electrical engineering](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering") together with a large cruising radius and extreme [seaworthiness](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Seakeeping "Seakeeping")."[[9]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:37-11):4

The Eighteenth Amendment was [repealed](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Repeal_of_Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Repeal of Prohibition in the United States") on 5 December 1933 with the [Twenty-first Amendment](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Twenty-first_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-first Amendment to the United States Constitution")[[10]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:3-12)—a little under a year before _Dione_ was commissioned.[[2]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:0-2) The cutter never operated in the capacity that she and her sister ships were constructed for: enforcing Prohibition in the United States.[[7]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/USCGC_Dione#cite_note-:28-8):166
